title: 652. London’s Golden Age: The Ghosts of Culloden (Part 3)

sentences.en: I had desired to visit the Hebrides or western islands of Scotland so long that I scarcely remember how the wish was originally excited and was, in the autumn of the year 1773,
sentences.zh: 我渴望访问苏格兰的赫布里底群岛或西部岛屿已经很久了，以至于我几乎记不清最初是因为什么而萌生了这个愿望；在1773年的秋天，

sentences.en: induced to undertake the journey by finding in Mr Boswell a companion whose acuteness would held my inquiry and whose gaiety of conversation and civility of manners
sentences.zh: 我决定动身成行，因为我发现波斯威尔先生是一位极佳的同伴，他的敏锐洞察力有助于我的考察，而他那妙趣横生的谈吐和彬彬有礼的举止

sentences.en: are sufficient to counteract the inconveniences of travel in countries less hospitable than we have passed.
sentences.zh: 足以抵消在一个远不如我们刚走过的那些地方那样好客的国家旅行所带来的种种不便。

sentences.en: On the 18th of August, we left Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 8月18日，我们离开了爱丁堡。

sentences.en: So that was the son of Litchfield, Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这就是利奇菲尔德之子，塞缪尔·约翰逊。

sentences.en: And he is describing one of the great journeys in all history, one of certainly the most intrepid journeys in all history.
sentences.zh: 他正在描述人类历史上的伟大远征之一，无疑也是历史上最无畏的远征之一。

sentences.en: And he's describing it in his book,
sentences.zh: 他正在他的书中记述这段旅程，

sentences.en: A Journey to the Western Islands of Scotland, which is actually one of the great classics of travel literature.
sentences.zh: 即《通往苏格兰西部群岛之旅》，这实际上是旅行文学中的伟大经典之一。

sentences.en: And Johnson, the ultimate Englishman, is describing how, for the first time in his life, he ventured beyond England's borders.
sentences.zh: 而作为终极英格兰人的约翰逊，正在记述他如何生平第一次冒险走出了英格兰的边界。

sentences.en: He goes up to the Hebrides, a journey that, in the 18th century, would have seemed to the average Englishman, especially a Midlander like Johnson,
sentences.zh: 他北上前往赫布里底群岛——在18世纪，对于普通英格兰人、尤其是像约翰逊这样的米德兰兹人来说，这趟旅程

sentences.en: to be going to the very ends of the earth, into the very heart of darkness and the den of savagery.
sentences.zh: 仿佛是要去往世界的尽头，深入黑暗的心脏和野蛮的巢穴。

sentences.en: Because, of course, you're going to the most Scottish place imaginable.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，你要去的是你能想象到的最苏格兰的地方。

sentences.en: So, Tom, the Western Islands.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，关于西部群岛。

sentences.en: Have you been to the Western Islands?
sentences.zh: 你去过西部群岛吗？

sentences.en: I have.
sentences.zh: 我去过。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Savage?
sentences.zh: 野蛮吗？

sentences.en: Wet is my chief memory of them.
sentences.zh: 我对其最主要的记忆是湿润。

sentences.en: I won't surprise people to hear, but very interesting for all the reasons that Johnson will be discovering and Boswell will be discovering.
sentences.zh: 听到这个大家可能不会感到意外，但由于约翰逊和波斯威尔即将发现的种种原因，这段经历非常有趣。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 那很好。

sentences.en: Because you mentioned how, to the average Englishman, the Western Isles, the Hebrides, are incredibly remote to Scots in the lowlands.
sentences.zh: 因为你提到过，对于普通英格兰人来说，西部群岛和赫布里底群岛对于低地苏格兰人而言是极其偏远的。

sentences.en: And this is something that Johnson points out in his book.
sentences.zh: 这也是约翰逊在他的书中指出的一个现象。

sentences.en: He says that to most lowlanders, they are as familiar with the Hebrides as they were with Borneo or Sumatra.
sentences.zh: 他说，对于大多数低地人来说，他们对赫布里底群岛的熟悉程度，就像他们对婆罗洲或苏门答腊一样。

sentences.en: And this is certainly true of James Boswell, the man mentioned by Johnson as his companion on this great adventure
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·波斯威尔也绝对如此——也就是约翰逊所说的陪伴他进行这次伟大冒险的同伴，

sentences.en: and whose escapades we were hearing about in our previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集中刚刚听过他的种种风流韵事。

sentences.en: And Boswell, too, you know, he's an inveterate journal writer.
sentences.zh: 而且波斯威尔也是个出了名的日记狂人。

sentences.en: And the journal that he writes on this trip provides him with the basis for his book, because he also gives an account of this journey, the Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides.
sentences.zh: 他在这次旅行中写的日记为他的书奠定了基础，因为他也对这次旅程做了记述，即《赫布里底群岛游记》。

sentences.en: And in his introduction to that book, he will spell out what the two men had been hoping to find in the Hebrides.
sentences.zh: 在该书的导言中，他详细阐述了这两个人一直希望在赫布里底群岛找到什么。

sentences.en: So you summed it up as savagery.
sentences.zh: 所以你把它总结为野蛮。

sentences.en: Boswell frames it slightly differently.
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔的表述则略有不同。

sentences.en: He says that they're looking for simplicity and wildness and all the circumstances of remote time or place so near to our native Great Island,
sentences.zh: 他说，他们寻找的是质朴、荒野，以及所有那些遥远时代或地方的环境，而这一切就存在于我们本土伟大的岛屿附近，

sentences.en: by which he means Great Britain, of course.
sentences.zh: 这里他指的当然是大不列颠。

sentences.en: So before we set off ourselves to the Hebrides for this extraordinary journey, a thrilling story, let us kick off in a place very close to your heart, Tom, Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们自己动身前往赫布里底群岛，开启这段非凡旅程和动人故事之前，让我们先从一个对你而言至关重要的地方——汤姆，爱丁堡——开始吧。

sentences.en: So Samuel Johnson has arrived for the first time in the Scottish capital.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊就这样首次抵达了苏格兰首府。

sentences.en: Remember, England and Scotland have only been united in one country since 1707.
sentences.zh: 记住，英格兰和苏格兰自1707年起才合并为一个国家。

sentences.en: So if you're quite old, that's within living memory on the 14th of August, 1773, which is where we kick off.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你年纪够大，在1773年8月14日——也就是我们启程的日子——这还在人们的亲身记忆之中。

sentences.en: And we're at Boyd's Inn, which is just off the Royal Mile in the heart of Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在博伊德客栈，它位于爱丁堡市中心皇家一英里大道旁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Samuel Johnson's arrival there is a great sensation in Edinburgh among polite circles, because he is by now one of the most famous people in the whole of Britain.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊的到来在爱丁堡的上流社交圈引起了极大的轰动，因为他当时已经是全英国最著名的人物之一。

sentences.en: The Great Cham, they call him, the name given to Tartar despots.
sentences.zh: 他们管他叫“大可汗”，这是给鞑靼专制君主的称号。

sentences.en: So he's the kind of the supreme monarch of literary Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以他某种程度上可以说是文学英国的至高君主。

sentences.en: And he is also, he's now 64, one of the most recognisable.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时64岁了，也是最容易被人认出来的人物之一。

sentences.en: And Boswell, in his Journal of a Tour to the Hebrides, prefaces it with a description of what Johnson looked like over the course of this trip.
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔在《赫布里底群岛游记》的前言中，对约翰逊在这次旅行中的外貌进行了描述。

sentences.en: So Boswell writes,
sentences.zh: 于是波斯威尔写道，

sentences.en: His person was a large, robust, I may say, approaching to the gigantic and grown unwieldy from corpulence.
sentences.zh: 他的身材高大、健硕，可以说接近巨人般魁梧，且因发福而显得笨重。

sentences.en: He has a convulsive twitch.
sentences.zh: 他有痉挛性的抽搐。

sentences.en: We've mentioned that.
sentences.zh: 我们提到过这一点。

sentences.en: He's constantly muttering to himself.
sentences.zh: 他经常自言自语。

sentences.en: And Boswell writes,
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔写道：

sentences.en: In the intervals of articulating, he made various sounds with his mouth, sometimes as if ruminating, or what is called chewing the cud, sometimes giving a half whistle,
sentences.zh: 在清晰说话的间隙，他的嘴里会发出各种声音，有时像是在反刍，也就是所谓的咀嚼反刍物，有时发出半声口哨，

sentences.en: sometimes making his tongue play backwards from the roof of his mouth, as if clucking like a hen.
sentences.zh: 有时让舌头在上颚后来回弹动，仿佛母鸡咯咯叫一样。

sentences.en: So he's unprepossessing company, a first appearance.
sentences.zh: 所以初次见面时，他并不是一个讨人喜欢的同伴。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, he's distinctive, I think it would be fair to say.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他很有特点，这么说算公道吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he's arrived in Scotland wearing his habitual brown suit, which he'd been wearing the first time that Boswell met him.
sentences.zh: 他到达苏格兰时穿着他那套习惯的棕色西装，这也是波斯威尔第一次见到他时穿的衣服。

sentences.en: And this time he has brought boots because he suspects it's going to be muddy.
sentences.zh: 而这一次他带了靴子，因为他猜可能会有泥泞。

sentences.en: It's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 他猜得没错。

sentences.en: He's got an enormous brown great coat, complete with kind of vast pockets.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件巨大的棕色长过膝大衣，带有那种巨大的口袋。

sentences.en: Boswell says he would have been able to fit his own dictionary in the pockets.
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔说，这口袋大得能塞进他自己编的词典。

sentences.en: And he's carrying a large English oak stick.
sentences.zh: 他手里拿着一根巨大的英国橡木手杖。

sentences.en: And he also has a pair of pistols with him and a supply of bullets.
sentences.zh: 他还随身携带了一副手枪和充足的子弹。

sentences.en: And this, as Boswell observed, from an erroneous apprehension of violence.
sentences.zh: 正如波斯威尔所观察到的，这是由于对暴力产生了错误的担忧。

sentences.en: So essentially, Johnson thinks the Highlands are going to be crawling with bandits, ruffians and ne'er-do-wells.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，约翰逊认为高地到处都是土匪、恶棍和无赖。

sentences.en: Bandits and ruffians and all kinds of people.
sentences.zh: 土匪、恶棍以及各种各样的人。

sentences.en: Now, I think that Johnson's critics would not have been surprised that he'd kind of basically come outfitted as John Bull.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想约翰逊的批评者们不会对他的这套装扮感到惊讶，因为他基本上把自己武装成了“约翰·布尔”的形象。

sentences.en: Because his public image is very much that of a little Englander, a man who essentially judges all the world by the standards of London.
sentences.zh: 因为他的公众形象非常符合一个“小英格兰人”的特征，一个基本上以伦敦的标准来衡量全世界的人。

sentences.en: You know, his famous saying, London is tired of life.
sentences.zh: 你知道他那句名言：厌倦了伦敦，就是厌倦了生活。

sentences.en: But Boswell knows Johnson very well and appreciates that this public image does not correspond to the private reality.
sentences.zh: 但波斯威尔非常了解约翰逊，并且明白这种公众形象与私底下的现实并不相符。

sentences.en: Because the reason that Johnson hasn't travelled is that for most of his life, he's been incredibly poor.
sentences.zh: 因为约翰逊没有去旅行的原因是，在他生命的绝大部分时间里，他穷得不可开交。

sentences.en: And travel is, relatively speaking, much more expensive in the 18th century than it is today.
sentences.zh: 而且相对而言，在18世纪，旅行的费用比今天要贵得多。

sentences.en: And Johnson, all his life, has had an incredibly frustrated yearning to see the world.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊一生中都有着一种受到极大压抑的渴望去看世界的愿望。

sentences.en: So he said of Italy, for instance, that, you know, basically a life without seeing Italy isn't a life worth living.
sentences.zh: 比如，他曾谈到意大利，说一个人如果不去看意大利，这一生就不算活过。

sentences.en: He's wanted to go to India.
sentences.zh: 他一直想去印度。

sentences.en: He has a particular thing about the Great Wall of China.
sentences.zh: 他对中国的万里长城有一种特别的执念。

sentences.en: Like Richard Nixon.
sentences.zh: 就像理查德·尼克松一样。

sentences.en: Well, Nixon gets to see it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，尼克松最终看到了它。

sentences.en: Johnson never did.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊至死也没有。

sentences.en: And so it's rather touching, actually, that in 1922, the first Viscount Rothermere, Dominic, so the ancestor of your erstwhile employers at the Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上挺让人感动的：在1922年，第一代罗瑟米尔子爵多米尼克——也就是你曾经的老板《每日邮报》报社创始人的先人……
zh_words: 罗瑟米尔子爵多米尼克

sentences.en: You're thinking about what to say there.
sentences.zh: 你在琢磨该说些什么。

sentences.en: I can see the cogs turning and you're thinking like you don't want to completely put yourself on the wrong side of the Rothermere organisation.
sentences.zh: 我能看出你脑子里在飞速运转，你既不想彻底把自己置于罗瑟米尔集团的对立面，

sentences.en: But equally, you don't want to put yourself on the wrong side of the listeners.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，你也不想站在听众的对立面。

sentences.en: What I will say in favour of the first Viscount Rothermere is that knowing of Johnson's yearning to see the Great Wall of China and knowing he's been frustrated,
sentences.zh: 我为第一代罗瑟米尔子爵说句公道话：由于知道约翰逊渴望看到万里长城却未能如愿，

sentences.en: he presented a stone from the Great Wall to Gough House, which was the house in which Johnson had written the dictionary, which you can still visit to this day.
sentences.zh: 他向高夫故居赠送了一块来自万里长城的石头——那是约翰逊编写词典的房子，你至今仍可以去那里参观。

sentences.en: Tremendous, a tremendous place.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，一个了不起的地方。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a lovely thing to have done.
sentences.zh: 哦，他做了一件多么美好的事啊。

sentences.en: So it has this stone from the Great Wall there.
sentences.zh: 所以那块来自万里长城的石头就在那里。

sentences.en: Yeah, great credit to Viscount Rothermere for that.
sentences.zh: 是的，罗瑟米尔子爵为此功不可没。

sentences.en: I think it's the only stone from the Great Wall in the whole of London.
sentences.zh: 我想这是整个伦敦唯一一块来自万里长城的石头。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太绝了。

sentences.en: That's an interesting fact.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有趣的事实。

sentences.en: And so Boswell knows this.
sentences.zh: 所以波斯威尔深知这一点。

sentences.en: And so this is why essentially he had been confident in urging Boswell to come to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么他基本上有信心力劝波斯威尔来到苏格兰。

sentences.en: Because he knows that Johnson specifically had wanted to see the Hebrides because Johnson had read about the Hebrides when he was a child.
sentences.zh: 因为他知道约翰逊特意想去看赫布里底群岛，是因为约翰逊在童年时期就读过关于那里的书。

sentences.en: And so it's a kind of childhood fantasy to go there.
sentences.zh: 所以去那里某种程度上可以说是他童年的幻想。

sentences.en: So Boswell comes scurrying along to this inn off the Royal Mile and he's delighted to see Johnson, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 于是波斯威尔匆忙赶到皇家一英里大道旁这家客栈，见到约翰逊时他很高兴，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's very excited.
sentences.zh: 他非常兴奋。

sentences.en: But he's a little bit nervous because he's worried that Johnson will embarrass him by bursting out, twitching and shouting his anti-Scottish prejudices, which would be very bad.
sentences.zh: 但他又有点紧张，因为他担心约翰逊会突然大喊大叫、身体抽搐并发表反苏格兰的偏见言论来让他难堪，那就太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Because Johnson is notorious for anti-Scottish prejudice.
sentences.zh: 因为约翰逊以持有反苏格兰偏见而闻名。

sentences.en: You know, he's always fulminating that Scotland's very poor, everyone eats oats, and that the Scots are forever fleeing Scotland for England.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他总是怒气冲冲地谴责苏格兰极度贫困、人人吃燕麦，还说苏格兰人总是逃离苏格兰前往英格兰。

sentences.en: And Boswell, of course, is an example of that.
sentences.zh: 而波斯威尔当然就是其中的一个例子。

sentences.en: So, as you say, Boswell is nervous.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，波斯威尔很紧张。

sentences.en: He takes Johnson by the arm.
sentences.zh: 他挽起约翰逊的手臂。

sentences.en: And so arm in arm, they walk up the Royal Mile towards his house, which is just off it.
sentences.zh: 于是他们手挽着手，沿著皇家一英里大道向他那座就在大道旁的房子走去。

sentences.en: And as they go, Boswell finds himself mortified by what he describes as the evening effluvia.
sentences.zh: 一路上，波斯威尔被他所形容的“晚间恶臭”折磨得羞愧难当。

sentences.en: So essentially the stench of drains.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是下水道的恶臭。

sentences.en: A zealous Scotsman would have wished Mr. Johnson to be without one of his five senses upon this occasion.
sentences.zh: 一个狂热的苏格兰人当时大概会希望约翰逊先生失去五官中的一种。

sentences.en: As we marched slowly along, he grumbled in my ear, I smell you in the dark.
sentences.zh: 当我们慢慢向前走时，他在我耳边咕哝着：我在黑暗中闻到你们的味道了。

sentences.en: So that's not a good start.
sentences.zh: 所以这可不是个好兆头。

sentences.en: And then two days later, there is going to be more hovrumphing because it's provoked by what remains, 64 years on, the single most controversial issue in Anglo-Scottish relations.
sentences.zh: 两天后，更多的抱怨声将会响起，因为这源于一个在64年后的今天依然是英苏关系中最具争议的话题。

sentences.en: And you just mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 而你刚好提到了它。

sentences.en: It's the Act of Union, which had dissolved the parliaments of England and Scotland and created a united kingdom of Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 这就是《联合条例》，它解散了英格兰和苏格兰的议会，创建了大不列颠联合王国。

sentences.en: And as you said, this act had been passed in 1707.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，这个法案是在1707年通过的。

sentences.en: And the Scottish Act of Union is kept in the Parliament House, which stands just off the Royal Mile by St. Giles Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 苏格兰的《联合条例》保存在议会大厦里，该大厦位于圣吉尔斯大教堂附近的皇家一英里大道旁。

sentences.en: And Boswell takes Johnson there and Johnson is shown the document.
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔带着约翰逊来到那里，文件被展示给约翰逊看。

sentences.en: And as Johnson is inspecting it, Boswell began in his own words to indulge old Scottish sentiments and to express a warm regret that by our union with England, we were no more.
sentences.zh: 正当约翰逊在仔细端详它时，波斯威尔用他自己的话说，开始沉浸于旧日的苏格兰情怀中，并对我们与英格兰合并导致我们不复存在表达了热烈的遗憾。

sentences.en: Ooh, the SNP enter the chat.
sentences.zh: 噢，苏格兰民族党（SNP）闪亮登场。

sentences.en: Boswell knows what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 波斯威尔知道自己在做什么。

sentences.en: He's winding Johnson up.
sentences.zh: 他在激怒约翰逊。

sentences.en: He knows that Johnson is going to explode.
sentences.zh: 他知道约翰逊要爆发了。

sentences.en: But Johnson responds in a perhaps unexpected way.
sentences.zh: 但约翰逊的反应却出乎意料。

sentences.en: So he's talking about Mary, Queen of Scots and saying that because the Scots hadn't tried to rescue her from captivity in England, therefore they don't deserve to be independent.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了苏格兰女王玛丽，并说因为苏格兰人没有试图把她从英格兰的囚禁中营救出来，所以他们不配独立。

sentences.en: Yeah, which is perhaps an argument that might defeat the SNP if it gets unleashed now.
sentences.zh: 是的，这或许是一个如果现在抛出来也能驳倒苏格兰民族党的论点。

sentences.en: I mean, who knows?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: And they're overheard, aren't they, by the keeper of the records or who's standing at their elbow?
sentences.zh: 他们被偷听到了，对吧，被档案管理员或者站在他们身旁的人？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he says a thing that you actually often hear, you often see online to this day.
sentences.zh: 然后那个人说了一句话，你现在在网上其实也经常听到、经常看到。

sentences.en: Half our nation was bribed by English money.
sentences.zh: 我们半个国家都被英国人的金钱收买了。

sentences.en: This is basically the sort of ultra Scottish nationalist take on Scottish history and on the Act of Union,
sentences.zh: 这基本上是极端苏格兰民族主义者对苏格兰历史和《联合条例》的看法，

sentences.en: saying that basically our elite were bribed by the English to sell our independence.
sentences.zh: 声称基本上是我们的精英被英国人收买，从而出卖了我们的独立。

sentences.en: And Johnson, brilliant answer.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊给出了绝妙的回答。

sentences.en: Sir, that's no defence that makes you worse.
sentences.zh: 先生，那不是辩护，那只会让你们显得更糟。

sentences.en: I mean, he's not wrong.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他说得没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To use the word we used in the very first episode, this is all very performative, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 借用我们在第一集里用过的一个词，这一切都非常具有表演性质，对吧？

sentences.en: They're basically going through the motions, having a bit of fun, playing their parts.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上只是走过场，找点乐子，扮演各自的角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's self-consciously banter, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一种自觉的玩笑，我认为。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's exactly what Boswell wanted, because then he can go back and write it up.
sentences.zh: 这正是波斯威尔想要的，因为这样他就可以回去把这些写下来。

sentences.en: And here we are talking about it all these years on.
sentences.zh: 而多年后的今天，我们正在谈论它。

sentences.en: But I think that Johnson's devotion to Mary, Queen of Scots, I mean, on one level, it seems a completely unexpected kind of tangent.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得约翰逊对苏格兰女王玛丽的忠诚，一方面似乎是一个完全出人意料的题外话，

sentences.en: But on the other, it's a reminder that there are actually much rawer and fresher political emotions kind of eddying around in Scotland than those generated by the Act of Union.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，它提醒我们，苏格兰周围回荡的政治情绪实际上比《联合条例》所产生的那些要更加原始和新鲜。

sentences.en: Three decades previously, so this is in 1745, the great, great, great grandson of Mary, Queen of Scots, Charles Stuart, who is better known as Bonny Prince Charlie,
sentences.zh: 三十年前，也就是1745年，苏格兰女王玛丽的玄孙查理·斯图亚特——也就是更广为人知的“英俊王子查理”——

sentences.en: he'd landed from France in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他从法国在苏格兰登陆。

sentences.en: And he had raised an army in the Highlands and led them southwards as far as Derby in the Midlands, so actually not far from Litchfield.
sentences.zh: 他在高地集结了一支军队，并率领他们一路向南打到米德兰兹的德比，实际上离利奇菲尔德并不远。

sentences.en: And Bonny Prince Charlie's aim was to overthrow the ruling British dynasty, the House of Hanover.
sentences.zh: 英俊王子查理的目标是推翻统治不列颠的汉诺威王朝。

sentences.en: And they were Protestants, the Stuarts are Catholic, and so the Protestant establishment had essentially brought in the House of Hanover to replace the Catholic House of Stuart.
sentences.zh: 他们是新教徒，而斯图亚特家族是天主教徒，因此新教当权派基本上引进了汉诺威王朝来取代天主教的斯图亚特王朝。

sentences.en: And this is why in the 18th century, you have kind of waves of King George's ruling all the time.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在18世纪，你总是会经历一波又一波的乔治国王统治。

sentences.en: And Bonny Prince Charlie wants to overthrow this and claim the throne for his father, King James III, as loyalists to Jacobus, as he's called in Latin, so Jacobites.
sentences.zh: 而查理王子想要推翻这一切，为他的父亲詹姆斯三世国王夺回王位，作为拉丁语中被称为雅各布斯（Jacobus）的人的忠实信徒，也就是所谓的詹姆斯党人。

sentences.en: Think of him.
sentences.zh: 想想看他。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, he can't reach London.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他无法抵达伦敦。

sentences.en: He retreats.
sentences.zh: 他撤退了。

sentences.en: He withdraws to the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 他退到了高地。

sentences.en: And there he is cornered at Culloden, a village by Inverness in the northeast corner of Scotland, and his army had been annihilated.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他在苏格兰东北角的因弗尼斯村庄卡洛丁被逼入绝境，他的军队被彻底消灭了。

sentences.en: And Bonny Prince Charlie had managed to escape the battlefield, but he has this completely hair-raising kind of flight across the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 查理王子虽然设法逃离了战场，但他却经历了一场令人毛骨悚然的高地大逃亡。

sentences.en: He gets to the Hebrides, and he only manages to get on board a ship and sail back to France by the absolute skin of his teeth.
sentences.zh: 他到达了赫布里底群岛，最终千钧一发地登上了一艘船，乘船返回了法国。

sentences.en: Now, three decades on from that great adventure, the prospects of the Stuarts returning to the British throne and replacing the Hanoverians are obviously, I mean, effectively zero.
sentences.zh: 如今，距离那场伟大的冒险已经过去了三十年，斯图尔特王朝重返英国王位并取代汉诺威王朝的前景，显而易见，或者说基本上是零。

sentences.en: But there are still those who preserve a wistful loyalty to them.
sentences.zh: 但仍然有人对他们怀有一丝依恋的忠诚。

sentences.en: And we mentioned in our very first episode how one of those is Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我们在第一集中提到过，其中一人就是塞缪尔·约翰逊。

sentences.en: Um, Boswell says, all his youth, he had felt a tenderness for that unfortunate house, so the Stuarts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，博斯韦尔说，他年轻时对那个不幸的家族，也就是斯图尔特家族，一直怀有一种温情。

sentences.en: That's a common thing among Tories.
sentences.zh: 这在托利党人中很常见。

sentences.en: So Tories had this kind of, um, this sort of nostalgic loyalty to the House of Stuart, didn't they?
sentences.zh: 所以托利党人对斯图尔特王朝有一种，嗯，这种怀旧式的忠诚，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Johnson, even as a young man, would have perhaps, maybe there's a slight element of affectation about it, but there so often is with political positions.
sentences.zh: 即使在约翰逊年轻的时候，他可能也会有这种倾向，也许其中带有轻微的矫情成分，但政治立场往往如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it doesn't undermine them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不损害他们的立场。

sentences.en: I mean, it's interesting you say that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你这么说很有意思。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's true to a degree.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为在某种程度上这是真的。

sentences.en: But in his life of Johnson, Boswell will point out that perhaps his affections might have gone beyond mere tenderness, because he writes that he's somewhat curious,
sentences.zh: 但在他的《约翰逊传》中，博斯韦尔指出，他的深情可能超越了单纯的温情，因为他写道，他感到有些奇怪的是，

sentences.en: that his literary career appears to have been almost totally suspended in the years 1745 and 1746.
sentences.zh: 在1745年和1746年间，他的文学生涯似乎几乎完全中断了。

sentences.en: So those are the years that Bonnie Prince Charlie is, you know, in Britain, trying to seize the throne.
sentences.zh: 所以，那正是查理王子在英国试图夺取王位的几年。

sentences.en: But wasn't he developing the idea of the dictionary at that point?
sentences.zh: 但当时他不是正在构思字典的想法吗？

sentences.en: So that's why he's so quiet.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他那么低调。

sentences.en: He definitely was by the time Culloden comes.
sentences.zh: 到卡洛丁战役爆发时，他绝对是在这么做。

sentences.en: Earlier, yeah, it's unclear.
sentences.zh: 至于更早的时候，是的，这并不清楚。

sentences.en: And there are a few scholars who suggest that perhaps he was actually embroiled in the campaign.
sentences.zh: 有一些学者认为，他实际上可能卷入了这场战役。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's unlikely.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得这不太可能。

sentences.en: I mean, he's the last person you'd want on your side, shambling with his massive pockets.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他拖着硕大的衣兜步履蹒跚，绝对是你最不想拉拢到自己阵营的人。

sentences.en: Yes, I think it's unlikely.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这不太可能。

sentences.en: But it's probable that he was lying low.
sentences.zh: 但他当时很可能是在低调行事、韬光养晦。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: He probably was known as a Jacobite, and so probably thought that, you know, it was sensible not to draw attention to it.
sentences.zh: 他当时可能被认为是一个詹姆斯党人，所以他大概觉得，你知道的，不引人注目是明智的。

sentences.en: Not anymore, though, right?
sentences.zh: 不过，现在不是了，对吧？

sentences.en: The king's, King George has given him a pension.
sentences.zh: 国王，乔治国王给了他一笔年金。

sentences.en: And didn't he meet the king in 1767, George III, at the library?
sentences.zh: 而且他不是在1767年在图书馆见过国王乔治三世吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, in the Royal Library at Windsor.
sentences.zh: 是的，在温莎的皇家图书馆里。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, Johnson's unapologetic about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，约翰逊对此并不感到抱歉。

sentences.en: We remember we discussed he he's been told this is pension is a kind of reward for doing the dictionary.
sentences.zh: 还记得我们讨论过吗，有人告诉他这笔年金是对他编写字典的一种奖励。

sentences.en: You don't have to serve as a kind of propagandist for the Hanoverians.
sentences.zh: 你不需要充当汉诺威王朝的宣传员。

sentences.en: But even so, I mean, Johnson appreciates, you know, as he says to Boswell, I cannot now curse the House of Hanover.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，约翰逊也意识到，正如他对博斯韦尔所说的那样，我现在不能诅咒汉诺威王朝了。

sentences.en: But he says that with a smile.
sentences.zh: 但他带着微笑说出了这句话。

sentences.en: I think that one of the reasons why Johnson does feel fondly towards Boswell is that he knows that Boswell also shares in these sympathies.
sentences.zh: 我认为约翰逊对博斯韦尔产生好感的原因之一，是他知道博斯韦尔也有同感。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Boswell's father, Lord Affleck, he's a Whig and he's a massive supporter of the House of Hanover.
sentences.zh: 所以，博斯韦尔的父亲奥斯利勋爵是个辉格党人，也是汉诺威王朝的坚定支持者。

sentences.en: Oh, right.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来如此。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: But Boswell, right from childhood, seems to have had this kind of romantic affection for Bonnie Prince Charlie.
sentences.zh: 但博斯韦尔从小似乎就对查理王子怀有一种浪漫的情愫。

sentences.en: And it may be, you know, so 1745, when Bonnie Prince Charlie lands, Boswell is four years old.
sentences.zh: 也许，你知道的，1745年查理王子登陆时，博斯韦尔才四岁。

sentences.en: And so this may be the first kind of political intervention that he's become aware of.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是他意识到的第一次政治介入。

sentences.en: Surely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 确实是的。

sentences.en: He clearly sees Bonnie Prince Charlie as a very romantic character and supports him,
sentences.zh: 他显然把查理王子看作是一个非常浪漫的人物并支持他，

sentences.en: even though it has to be said he's offered a coin by a servant if he will shout God save King George, which he takes and he does shout it.
sentences.zh: 尽管不得不说，曾有个仆人对他说，如果他高呼“上帝保佑国王乔治”，就会给他一枚硬币，他拿了硬币也确实喊了。

sentences.en: But having pocketed it, he then goes back to his kind of Jacobite sympathies.
sentences.zh: 但把钱放进兜里后，他又回到了他那类詹姆斯党人的同情倾向中。

sentences.en: He basically stays loyal in a kind of, as you say, slightly performative way for all his life.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他基本上以一种略带表演性质的方式，一生都保持着忠诚。

sentences.en: And actually, when he was in Corsica, he had kind of mad fantasies about maybe seeing the Stuarts established on the island of Corsica.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当他在科西嘉岛时，他曾有一种疯狂的幻想，也许能看到斯图尔特家族在科西嘉岛建立政权。

sentences.en: That completely should have happened.
sentences.zh: 那绝对是应该发生的。

sentences.en: Should that not have happened?
sentences.zh: 难道不应该发生吗？

sentences.en: The Stuart Kingdom of Corsica?
sentences.zh: 斯图尔特科西嘉王国？

sentences.en: Well, if history is great, great what ifs, it would have stopped Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果历史充满了伟大的假设，那本可以阻止拿破仑。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think that, obviously, Johnson and Boswell do have this fascination.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，很明显，约翰逊和博斯韦尔确实有着这种迷恋。

sentences.en: And by this point, it may be nothing more than that with Bonnie Prince Charlie.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，这可能不过是对查理王子的迷恋罢了。

sentences.en: You know, the whole story, it's very romantic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，整个故事非常浪漫。

sentences.en: His defeat at Culloden, his escape across the Highlands, you know, the fact he takes refuge on the Hebrides.
sentences.zh: 他在卡洛丁的战败，他穿过高地的逃亡，你知道的，他以赫布里底群岛为避难所的事实。

sentences.en: And I think it is definitely an important motivator for both of them in making this trip.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对是他们俩进行这次旅行的一个重要动因。

sentences.en: And I think it also helps to explain the route that they end up taking, because the obvious route to the Western Isles from Edinburgh is, duh, to go westwards.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这也解释了他们最终选择的路线，因为从爱丁堡去往西部群岛显而易见的路线是，呃，向西走。

sentences.en: But Johnson and Boswell opt instead to take a much more roundabout route.
sentences.zh: 但约翰逊和博斯韦尔选择了一条更为迂回的路线。

sentences.en: And they take the eastern road out of Scotland, up the coast, going northwards towards Inverness.
sentences.zh: 他们走的是离开苏格兰的东部公路，沿着海岸向北前往因弗尼斯。

sentences.en: And Inverness, of course, is a place that is very close to Culloden.
sentences.zh: 当然，因弗尼斯是一个离卡洛丁非常近的地方。

sentences.en: And to get from Inverness, they'll be going down Loch Ness and then across the hills and across the sea to the Western Isles.
sentences.zh: 从因弗尼斯出发，他们将沿尼斯湖而下，然后穿过群山，跨越大海前往西部群岛。

sentences.en: That is basically the route that Bonnie Prince Charlie had taken.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是查理王子走过的路线。

sentences.en: And it's incredibly picturesque.
sentences.zh: 而且极其风景如画。

sentences.en: I mean, it's ticking every box, that route.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那条路线符合所有的条件。

sentences.en: Do you think it is a sort of a Jacobite tour for them?
sentences.zh: 你认为这算是一种他们的詹姆斯党之旅吗？

sentences.en: I mean, genuinely, they've designed it accordingly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，真的，他们就是这样设计的。

sentences.en: I think so, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 真不错。

sentences.en: It's one of many factors.
sentences.zh: 这是众多因素之一。

sentences.en: But I think for both of them,
sentences.zh: 但我认为对他们两个来说，

sentences.en: the sense of the romance in Bonnie Prince Charlie's story lends an extra patina of excitement to the scenes that they're going to be seeing in the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 查理王子故事中的浪漫感为他们即将在高地看到的景色增添了一层额外的兴奋色彩。

sentences.en: I think absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我完全赞同。

sentences.en: Excitingly for them, they will also get to visit one of my alma martyrs, whatever the plural of alma martyrs.
sentences.zh: 令他们兴奋的是，他们还将参观我的母校之一（alma mater的复数形式是什么来着）。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 圣安德鲁斯。

sentences.en: St. Andrews.
sentences.zh: 圣安德鲁斯。

sentences.en: So, very exciting.
sentences.zh: 所以，非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So, they're about to set off.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们即将出发。

sentences.en: Johnson has had a tremendous time in Edinburgh, hasn't he?
sentences.zh: 约翰逊在爱丁堡度过了一段美妙的时光，不是吗？

sentences.en: He actually liked it, despite the stench.
sentences.zh: 尽管有恶臭，他其实还是挺喜欢那里的。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他是的。

sentences.en: So, he keeps landing what Boswell calls his pleasant hits against Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以，他不断抛出博斯韦尔所说的对苏格兰的善意调侃。

sentences.en: But actually, he's pretty well behaved.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他表现得相当规矩。

sentences.en: He's genuinely impressed by the beauties of Edinburgh and its architecture.
sentences.zh: 他真心对爱丁堡的美景及其建筑印象深刻。

sentences.en: And he's very flattered by the kind of the great host of Edinburgh luminaries who come to visit him in Boswell's house, really enjoys their company.
sentences.zh: 而且，大批来到博斯韦尔家中拜访他的爱丁堡名流让他感到十分荣幸，他真的很享受他们的陪伴。

sentences.en: And, of course, Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 当然还有爱丁堡。

sentences.en: I mean, Edinburgh is not an intellectual backwater.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，爱丁堡并不是一个思想文化落后的地方。

sentences.en: This is the great age of the Scottish Enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 这是苏格兰启蒙运动的伟大时代。

sentences.en: And there are lots of people who it's well worth Johnson meeting.
sentences.zh: 这里有许多非常值得约翰逊去拜访的人。

sentences.en: So, he, I think, really enjoys Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为他是真的很享受爱丁堡。

sentences.en: Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 爱丁堡。

sentences.en: They leave Edinburgh on the 18th of August and they have with them a single servant who is absolutely massive Bohemian, very well travelled, speaks lots of languages.
sentences.zh: 他们于8月18日离开爱丁堡，随身带着一个单身仆人，那人是个身材魁梧的波西米亚人，见多识广，精通多种语言。

sentences.en: Frederick the Great would have loved him, would have enrolled him in his army.
sentences.zh: 腓特烈大帝一定会喜欢他，并把他招入军队。

sentences.en: They obviously want someone who's huge because Johnson is clearly still a bit nervous about what they're going to be finding in the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 他们显然需要一个身材高大的人，因为约翰逊对他们将在高地发现什么显然仍然有些紧张。

sentences.en: So, they leave Edinburgh, as I say, they're heading eastwards and they head for St Andrews, Scotland's oldest university and a city described by Johnson as once arch-episcopal,
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我所说，他们离开爱丁堡，向东进发，前往苏格兰最古老的大学所在地圣安德鲁斯，这座城市被约翰逊形容为曾经的大主教驻地，

sentences.en: meaning there had once been an archbishop there, but the Scottish Reformation had then destroyed it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着那里曾经有一位大主教，但随后的苏格兰宗教改革将其摧毁了。

sentences.en: And Johnson does not approve of this at all and thinks that John Knox is an absolutely terrible man and laments it.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊对此完全不予赞同，认为约翰·诺克斯绝对是个糟糕透顶的人，并对此感到痛心。

sentences.en: He's treated very well, again, by the professors, all of whom are thrilled to meet him, but he does find the city unhappily declined.
sentences.zh: 教授们对他的态度非常好，所有人都为能见到他而激动不已，但他确实发现这座城市不幸地衰落了。

sentences.en: So, he writes, one of its streets is now lost and in those that remain there is the silence and solitude of inactive indigence and gloomy depopulation.
sentences.zh: 因此他写道，它的一条街道现在已经消失了，而在剩下的街道里，则弥漫着不活跃的贫困与阴暗的人口减少所带来的寂静与孤独。

sentences.en: There is something quite gloomy about St Andrews.
sentences.zh: 圣安德鲁斯有一种相当阴暗的氛围。

sentences.en: So, it's out on the east coast of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 它位于苏格兰东海岸。

sentences.en: You've got nothing between you and the kind of Siberian winds.
sentences.zh: 除了你和西伯利亚寒风之间，什么也没有。

sentences.en: It can be very cold and you're a long way from anywhere.
sentences.zh: 那里会非常冷，而且离任何地方都很远。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think for Johnson, though, it's not just that, you know, there are the ruins of, you know, bare-ruined choirs and all of that, the marks of the Scottish Reformation.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为对约翰逊来说，不仅仅是因为那里有诸如残垣断壁的诗诗歌歌之类苏格兰宗教改革的痕迹，

sentences.en: It's also that it does seem to be very depopulated.
sentences.zh: 还因为它似乎确实人口稀少。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's clearly not as flourishing as it once was.
sentences.zh: 它显然不像过去那样繁荣了。

sentences.en: And this will become one of the great themes of his book on the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 这将成为他关于高地的著作中的一大主题。

sentences.en: The sense that there are parts of Scotland, the lowlands, that are absolutely booming, but there are other parts, and particularly the more northerly reaches, that are clearly not.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉是，苏格兰的某些地方，比如低地，正在绝对繁荣发展，但其他地方，特别是更靠北的地区，则显然没有。

sentences.en: And the whole trip, Johnson is brooding on this.
sentences.zh: 在整个旅程中，约翰逊一直在沉思这一点。

sentences.en: And actually, he has a lot of time to think because the journey is quite a long one.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他有很多时间思考，因为行程相当漫长。

sentences.en: And going from St. Andrews up towards Aberdeen, you know, the coach is kind of bumping around on the roads.
sentences.zh: 从圣安德鲁斯到阿伯丁，你知道的，马车在路上颠簸着。

sentences.en: And Johnson, who isn't usually a man to complain, but he is, I think, slightly feeling his age.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊平时并不是一个爱抱怨的人，但我想他多少有点感到自己岁数大了。

sentences.en: And there's one particularly long and dreary stretch of road in the approaches to Aberdeen.
sentences.zh: 在接近阿伯丁的路上，有一段特别长且单调乏味的公路。

sentences.en: He goes so far as to worry about how on earth he is going to cope riding a horse.
sentences.zh: 他甚至开始担心自己究竟该怎么骑马。

sentences.en: And he tells Boswell, if we must ride much, we shall not go, and there's an end on it.
sentences.zh: 他对博斯韦尔说，如果我们必须骑很多路，那我们就不去了，事情就这么结束了。

sentences.en: And I have to say that there's an end on it is one of my favourite phrases from Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我必须说“事情就这么结束了”是约翰逊我最喜欢的短语之一。

sentences.en: But the next day, he's cheered up, and Boswell joshes him about the fact that he'd been, you know, worrying about horses and kind of always lapsing into self-pity.
sentences.zh: 但第二天，他的精神振作起来了，博斯韦尔开玩笑说他曾担心马匹并总是陷入自怜之中。

sentences.en: He says, why, sir, you was beginning to despond yesterday.
sentences.zh: 他说，怎么，先生，你昨天开始沮丧了。

sentences.en: You're a delicate Londoner.
sentences.zh: 你是个娇气的伦敦人。

sentences.en: You're a macaroni.
sentences.zh: 你是个花花公子。

sentences.en: You can't ride.
sentences.zh: 你根本不会骑马。

sentences.en: Oh, that's great banter.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是极好的玩笑。

sentences.en: So Johnson would absolutely despise, he would, I mean, that would force him to ride.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰逊绝对会鄙视这一点，我的意思是，这会逼得他去骑马。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's not going to, he's not going to take being called a macaroni.
sentences.zh: 他绝不会容忍别人叫他花花公子。

sentences.en: No, because macaronis are people who dress in exaggerated Italian fashions with enormous wigs.
sentences.zh: 对的，因为花花公子是指那些穿着夸张的意大利时装、戴着巨大假发的人。

sentences.en: That's not Johnson's vibe at all.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是约翰逊的风格。

sentences.en: And Johnson is very indignant about it.
sentences.zh: 对此，约翰逊感到非常愤慨。

sentences.en: Sir, I shall ride better than you.
sentences.zh: 先生，我骑得会比你好。

sentences.en: I was only afraid I should not find a horse able to carry me.
sentences.zh: 我只是担心找不到一匹能驮得动我的马。

sentences.en: Which has to be said, it is a reasonable worry because he is, as we say, enormous by this point.
sentences.zh: 不得不说，这是一个合理的担心，因为正如我们所说，他此时体型极为庞大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that evening they arrive in Aberdeen.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚，他们抵达了阿伯丁。

sentences.en: They get to the inn.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了客栈。

sentences.en: The inn is full.
sentences.zh: 客栈客满。

sentences.en: Boswell mentions his family name and immediately a room is found for them.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔报出了他的家族姓氏，随即就为他们腾出一个房间。

sentences.en: So that's a measure of the reputation, if not of Boswell himself, of his father, Lord Affleck.
sentences.zh: 这不仅体现了博斯韦尔本人的声誉，也体现了他的父亲奥斯利勋爵的声誉。

sentences.en: And the next day in Aberdeen, Johnson gets lionized again.
sentences.zh: 第二天在阿伯丁，约翰逊再次受到英雄般的捧场。

sentences.en: And the city elders are so excited to have him in their presence that they actually vote in the freedom of the city.
sentences.zh: 城市长老们对他的到来兴奋不已，甚至投票授予了他城市荣誉市民身份。

sentences.en: So Johnson is now in a much better mood.
sentences.zh: 所以约翰逊现在的心情好多了。

sentences.en: And what is more, they are now starting to approach the sublime kind of landscape that he's been hoping for.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，他们现在开始接近他一直期盼的那种崇高的风景。

sentences.en: Because to quote Boswell, he always said that he was not come to Scotland to see fine places of which there were enough in England.
sentences.zh: 因为用博斯韦尔的话来说，他总是说他来苏格兰不是为了看美丽的风景，英格兰的美景已经够多了。

sentences.en: But wild objects, mountains, waterfalls, peculiar manners.
sentences.zh: 而是为了看狂野的景物、山脉、瀑布和独特的风俗。

sentences.en: So, again, there's that sense of romanticism, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 所以，这里又有一种浪漫主义的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: The love of the kind of savage and the wildness and all of that kind of thing, you know, casting off the veneer of the city and getting into nature.
sentences.zh: 对那种野蛮、荒凉以及诸如此类事物的热爱，你知道的，抛开城市的浮华，投入大自然的怀抱。

sentences.en: Yeah, and Johnson is often thought as a kind of, you know, classical figure, you know, his Latin and his love of London and all of that.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们通常把约翰逊看作是一个，你知道的，古典主义人物，你知道的，他的拉丁文、他对伦敦的热爱以及诸如此类。

sentences.en: But he has come to Scotland to see wilderness.
sentences.zh: 但他来到苏格兰是为了看荒野。

sentences.en: And so wilderness he is going to see.
sentences.zh: 所以他将看到荒野。

sentences.en: And there's a taster for Boswell of how potentially alarming this enthusiasm for wild scenery might be.
sentences.zh: 这对于博斯韦尔来说算是一个试水，让他预见这种对狂野风景的热情可能会带来多大的惊吓。

sentences.en: Because they visit the Bullers of Buchan, which is a wild coastal walk that goes around very boiling waters known locally as the pot.
sentences.zh: 因为他们参观了布坎布勒斯，那是一条狂野的海岸步道，周围是当地人称为“壶穴”的汹涌水域。

sentences.en: And Boswell, actually, I mean, he's terrified to see the hugely corpulent Johnson kind of striding along this rocky ledge with grim rocks and boiling waters below him.
sentences.zh: 说实话，博斯韦尔，我的意思是，他看到身材极其庞大的约翰逊迈着步子走在这个岩石峭壁上时，吓坏了，下面就是严酷的岩石和汹涌的河水。

sentences.en: It was rather alarming to see Mr. Johnson poking his way.
sentences.zh: 看到约翰逊先生摸索着前行，着实让人捏一把汗。

sentences.en: And I guess Boswell is thinking, well, how's it going to play if, you know, the greatest man of British letters plunges to his death?
sentences.zh: 我猜博斯韦尔在想，好吧，如果这位英国文学界最伟大的人物一不小心失足坠亡，这局面该怎么收场？

sentences.en: That's not going to be a good look at all.
sentences.zh: 那可真是一点都不好看。

sentences.en: Anyway, Johnson survives it and gets in the coach and he's very happy.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，约翰逊挺了过来，上了马车，他非常高兴。

sentences.en: But Boswell, I think, reflecting on the possibility of Johnson falling to his death, he's suddenly become prey to gloomy fancies.
sentences.zh: 但我想，博斯韦尔在反思约翰逊坠崖身亡的可能性时，突然陷入了悲观的幻想之中。

sentences.en: And the landscape and the literary associations around Inverness kind of play on his fears.
sentences.zh: 因弗内斯周围的风景和文学联想进一步加剧了他的恐惧。

sentences.en: So by the afternoon of the 26th of August, they're driving across the heath where Macbeth was supposed to have met the three witches at the start of Shakespeare's play.
sentences.zh: 所以在8月26日下午，他们驾车穿过荒原，莎士比亚戏剧开头中，麦克白就是在那里遇到了三个女巫。

sentences.en: And Boswell finds himself shivering in terror and he's working himself up into an absolute state.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔发现自己吓得瑟瑟发抖，情绪也变得极度紧张。

sentences.en: And then as they're rattling along across this heath, they see the rotting body of a highwayman in a gibbet.
sentences.zh: 然后，当他们沿着这片荒原颠簸前行时，他们看到了一个吊在绞架上的江洋大盗腐烂的尸体。

sentences.en: The highwayman has been there for two months.
sentences.zh: 这个江洋大盗已经挂在那里两个月了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Boswell, he describes it as that strange curiosity, which I always have about anything dismal, climbs out of the coach and inspects it.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔把他对任何阴暗事物一贯的那种奇异好奇心描述为，他爬出马车并对其进行了检查。

sentences.en: And it has to be said that Boswell has quite a thing about hangings.
sentences.zh: 必须得说，博斯韦尔对绞刑有着相当狂热的兴趣。

sentences.en: It isn't, I think, because he's a sadist or anything like this.
sentences.zh: 我想这并不是因为他是个虐待狂或者别的什么。

sentences.en: I think it's actually the opposite.
sentences.zh: 我认为恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I think it's because he is oppressed by mortality and kind of dares himself to stare it in the face.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为他被对死亡的恐惧所压倒，从而敢于直视死亡。

sentences.en: He would go and talk to people who are about to be hanged and then watch them be hanged and then inspect their bodies afterwards.
sentences.zh: 他会去和即将被绞死的人交谈，然后观看他们被绞死，接着在事后检查他们的尸体。

sentences.en: And it's kind of staring the inevitability of death in the face, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想，这有点像直视死亡的不可避免性。

sentences.en: And so his response to this often, I mean, here it gets even weirder.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此的反应通常是，我的意思是，这里甚至变得更加诡异。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Is that he would go out and have sex with a prostitute, I think, to feel alive.
sentences.zh: 那就是他会出去和妓女发生性关系，我想，是为了感受活着的感觉。

sentences.en: And obviously the very deep waters there.
sentences.zh: 很显然那里的水非常深。

sentences.en: But also Boswell does that.
sentences.zh: 但博斯韦尔也确实会这么做。

sentences.en: I mean, his response to anything.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他对任何事情的反应。

sentences.en: I mean, his response to the death of his mum was to go to a brothel, no?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他对他母亲去世的反应竟然是去妓院，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我是说。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: I mean, but this, I think, is what makes him such a fascinating man, is that he has all these kind of strange takes on life, these strange approaches, these strange emotions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但这也正是让他成为一个如此迷人的人的原因，那就是他对生活有着所有这些奇怪的看法、奇怪的方法、奇怪的情感。

sentences.en: But he just writes them up.
sentences.zh: 但他只是把它们写了下来。

sentences.en: Strange approaches that always somehow come back to the same destination.
sentences.zh: 这些奇怪的方法总是不知何故回到了同一个终点。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, that is one destination.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，那是一个终点。

sentences.en: But another destination, as we say, is this kind of, this kind of enthusiasm almost for working himself up into a state of terror and dread of death.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，另一个终点是，对将自己陷入恐惧和对死亡的恐惧状态中几乎抱有这种热情。

sentences.en: And that evening he is, you know, completely morbid.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，你知道的，他完全陷入了病态。

sentences.en: And Johnson either doesn't recognise it or wants to tweak Boswell's tale.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊要么没有察觉到这一点，要么就是想捉弄一下博斯韦尔。

sentences.en: So Boswell writes that Mr. Johnson did not know of my, you know, basically the fact that I was in a massive funk.
sentences.zh: 所以博斯韦尔写道，约翰逊先生并不知道我，你知道的，基本上是我当时陷入了极度恐慌的事实。

sentences.en: Or, he told me afterwards, he would not have talked as he did, for he diverted himself with trying to frighten me as if the witches would come and dance at the foot of my bed.
sentences.zh: 或者，他事后告诉我，他不会那样说话，因为他通过试图吓唬我来消磨时间，就好像女巫会来到我的床头跳舞一样。

sentences.en: So you can imagine, you know, Johnson basically telling Boswell lots of ghost stories.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，你知道的，约翰逊基本上给博斯韦尔讲了许多鬼故事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Boswell kind of gibbering in his bed.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在床上吓得语无伦次。

sentences.en: So if you're into ghosts and death, two very exciting places to come.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你喜欢鬼魂和死亡，这里有两个非常刺激的地方可以来。

sentences.en: So on the road to Inverness, two more big sites to look at.
sentences.zh: 所以在去因弗内斯的路上，还有两个重要的景点值得一看。

sentences.en: One of them is Macbeth's Castle, so the Castle of Cawdor.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是麦克白的城堡，也就是考多城堡。

sentences.en: And the other is the Battlefield of Culloden, which we've already heard about.
sentences.zh: 另一个是卡洛登战场，我们之前已经听说过了。

sentences.en: So let's start with Macbeth's Castle.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们从麦克白的城堡开始吧。

sentences.en: So they do visit Macbeth's Castle.
sentences.zh: 他们确实参观了麦克白的城堡。

sentences.en: Its own, I mean, how does that work in those days?
sentences.zh: 它本身的，我的意思是，在那些日子里这是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: Somebody must live there or is it ruined?
sentences.zh: 一定有人住在那里还是说它已经成了废墟？

sentences.en: It's ruined, but there's a local minister who entertains them.
sentences.zh: 它成了废墟，但有一位当地的牧师在那里接待他们。

sentences.en: And they go and inspect the castle and Boswell is delighted by it, not by the castle itself so much.
sentences.zh: 他们去参观了城堡，博斯韦尔对此感到非常高兴，倒不是因为城堡本身。

sentences.en: It's a spectacle of Mr. Samuel Johnson in this remote place with all its literary associations.
sentences.zh: 而是塞缪尔·约翰逊先生身处这个偏远地方，并带着所有文学联想的景象。

sentences.en: And in fact, he wrote a letter to David Garrick, the great actor, that very evening.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在那天晚上，他给伟大演员大卫·加里克写了一封信。

sentences.en: Indeed, as I have always been accustomed to view him, Dr. Johnson, as a permanent London object,
sentences.zh: 的确，正如我一直习惯将他——约翰逊博士——视为伦敦的一个常驻地标一样，

sentences.en: it would not be much more wonderful to me to see St. Paul's Church moving along where we now are.
sentences.zh: 看到圣保罗大教堂移动到我们现在所在的这个地方，对我来说并没有显得更加神奇。

sentences.en: And I think you have this sense throughout the trip that Boswell is almost like a kind of documentary director.
sentences.zh: 我想在整个旅程中你都会有这种感觉，博斯韦尔几乎就像是一个纪录片导演。

sentences.en: He's removed someone from his comfortable surroundings and placed him in a locale where all kinds of adventures might ensue.
sentences.zh: 他把一个人从舒适的环境中带出来，放到一个可能会发生各种冒险的地方。

sentences.en: And he's always kind of framing Johnson in his mind.
sentences.zh: 而且他总是在脑海中构图约翰逊。

sentences.en: I have a friend called Rory who once took Dennis Rodman to North Korea.
sentences.zh: 我有一个叫罗里的朋友，他曾经带丹尼斯·罗德曼去过朝鲜。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And he stayed there, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 他还在那儿呆过，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They hung around.
sentences.zh: 他们到处闲逛。

sentences.en: It was a promotional thing for Paddy Power, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这是为Paddy Power做的宣传活动。

sentences.en: So improbable.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, but no more improbable than Samuel Johnson going to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，但并不比塞缪尔·约翰逊去苏格兰更不可思议。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so this is a crucial part of Boswell's delight in the whole trip.
sentences.zh: 所以这是博斯韦尔对整个旅程感到兴奋的一个关键部分。

sentences.en: So they get to see the castle at Cawdor.
sentences.zh: 于是他们得以参观考多城堡。

sentences.en: Or they do not go to inspect the battlefield of Culloden.
sentences.zh: 或者说他们没有去参观卡洛登战场。

sentences.en: And I think there are various reasons for this.
sentences.zh: 我想这其中有各种各样的原因。

sentences.en: Firstly, it's off the road.
sentences.zh: 首先，它不在大路上。

sentences.en: And Johnson isn't a man for taking, I think, a hike across Scottish Heather.
sentences.zh: 而且约翰逊可不是那种会选择在苏格兰石楠花丛中徒步的人。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: They don't have horses that they could ride.
sentences.zh: 他们没有可以骑的马。

sentences.en: And it's a very, very sensitive location.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个非常非常敏感的地点。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's a little bit like, I don't know, poking around a nuclear facility in Iran.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，这有点像，我不知道，在伊朗的核设施周围闲逛。

sentences.en: It's probably not the most sensible thing to do if you're a touriSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个游客，这可能不是最明智的做法。

sentences.en: But it's clear that the history of Bonnie Prince Charlie is very much on their minds now because they arrive in Inverness and then the next day they make a point of visiting this Fort George,
sentences.zh: 但很明显，邦尼·查理王子（小王子）的历史现在非常深刻地印在他们的脑海里，因为他们抵达了因弗内斯，然后第二天他们特意去参观了这个乔治堡，

sentences.en: which is this fortress that had been built in the wake of Culloden to kind of pacify the highlands.
sentences.zh: 这是在卡洛登战役之后建造的一座堡垒，旨在安抚高地。

sentences.en: So it's at one end of Loch Ness and Fort Augustus is at the other end of Loch Ness.
sentences.zh: 所以它在尼斯湖的一端，而奥古斯都堡在尼斯湖的另一端。

sentences.en: They're very excited by now because they know that they are going to be following the line of Loch Ness and they're going to be heading out into a country upon which,
sentences.zh: 他们现在非常兴奋，因为他们知道他们将沿着尼斯湖的路线前进，他们将前往一片，正如约翰逊所说，

sentences.en: as Johnson puts it, perhaps no wheel has ever rolled.
sentences.zh: 可能从未有车轮碾过的地方。

sentences.en: And so they buy four horses, one for Johnson, one for Boswell, one for Ritter, their giant bohemian manservant.
sentences.zh: 于是他们买了四匹马，一匹给约翰逊，一匹给博斯韦尔，一匹给丽特，他们那个身材高大的波希米亚男仆。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: I forgot he was there.
sentences.zh: 我忘了他在那儿了。

sentences.en: And a fourth to carry their baggage.
sentences.zh: 第四匹用来驮行李。

sentences.en: And that evening, they're last for a while in civilised company.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，他们在文明社会的陪伴下度过了最后一段时光。

sentences.en: They're in an inn in Inverness, all kinds of, you know, as usually happens, luminaries have turned up to have a gawp at Dr. Johnson and listen to his conversations.
sentences.zh: 他们在因弗内斯的一家客栈里，各种各样的人，你知道的，就像通常发生的那样，名流们纷纷赶来围观约翰逊博士并聆听他的谈话。

sentences.en: And Johnson is in excellent form and they're discussing the state of the world and the name of Joseph Banks comes up because the backdrop to this is that Captain Cook has just returned from his trip around the world,
sentences.zh: 约翰逊状态极佳，他们正在讨论世界的现状，约瑟夫·班克斯的名字被提了出来，因为这背后的背景是库克船长刚刚结束了他的环球旅行，

sentences.en: their trip to Australia with the goat.
sentences.zh: 他们带着山羊去澳大利亚的旅行。

sentences.en: Johnson had actually written the poem in Latin saluting the goat and he's friends with Banks.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊实际上曾用拉丁语写过一首诗向这只山羊致敬，而且他和班克斯是朋友。

sentences.en: And he reveals that Banks in Australia had seen a really remarkable animal, which Banks terms a kangaroo.
sentences.zh: 他透露，班克斯在澳大利亚看到了一种非常奇特的动物，班克斯称之为袋鼠。

sentences.en: And people say, well, what does this kangaroo look like?
sentences.zh: 人们问，嗯，这只袋鼠长什么样？

sentences.en: And Johnson, this incredibly eminent, this incredibly distinguished, this incredibly heavy man, rises to his feet.
sentences.zh: 然后约翰逊，这位极其杰出、极其卓越、体型极其庞大的人，站了起来。

sentences.en: He stood erect, put out his hands like feelers and gathering up the tails of his huge brown coat so as to resemble the pouch of the animal,
sentences.zh: 他挺直身子，把双手像触角一样伸出来，并把他的那件巨大的棕色外套的下摆聚拢起来，以模仿这种动物的育儿袋，

sentences.en: made two or three vigorous bounds across the room.
sentences.zh: 在房间里充满活力地蹦跳了两三下。

sentences.en: So the first kangaroo impersonation we've had on the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在节目中迎来了第一次袋鼠模仿秀，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: But ahead has even greater excitement because we've talked about one exotic and improbable creature in a kangaroo and we might just be about to meet another because after the break,
sentences.zh: 但前方还有更大的兴奋，因为我们已经讨论了一种异国情调且不可思议的生物——袋鼠，我们可能很快就要见到另一种了，因为休息过后，

sentences.en: Johnson and Boswell will be going to Loch Ness.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊和博斯韦尔将前往尼斯湖。

sentences.en: We would need to understand the policy context.
sentences.zh: 我们需要理解政策背景。

sentences.en: All the relevant context will be structured as a framework today and disseminated into an operation order.
sentences.zh: 所有相关的背景今天都将被构建为一个框架，并分发到作战命令中。

sentences.en: Or Frago?
sentences.zh: 或者说前线作战命令？

sentences.en: A Frago that says to kill the president of Russia.
sentences.zh: 一份下令刺杀俄罗斯总统的前线作战命令。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: New from Goalhanger.
sentences.zh: 来自Goalhanger的新节目。

sentences.en: Who is going to be able to pull this off?
sentences.zh: 谁能完成这个任务？

sentences.en: Sergeant Tom McDuff!
sentences.zh: 汤姆·麦克达夫中士！

sentences.en: Duffy!
sentences.zh: 达菲！

sentences.en: An audio drama journey like no other.
sentences.zh: 无与伦比的有声剧之旅。

sentences.en: Men like Duffy, they are our most valuable weapons.
sentences.zh: 像达菲这样的人，是我们最宝贵的武器。

sentences.en: Devised as a technically rigorous geopolitical action thriller.
sentences.zh: 被构想为一部技术严谨的地缘政治动作惊悚片。

sentences.en: We have two times friendly key.
sentences.zh: 我们有两次友军密钥。

sentences.en: Where Britain plays its strongest hand.
sentences.zh: 英国打出了他最强的一手牌。

sentences.en: He's the beSt.
sentences.zh: 他是最棒的。

sentences.en: Against its strongest foe.
sentences.zh: 对抗他最强大的敌人。

sentences.en: Bear Hunt.
sentences.zh: 猎熊行动。

sentences.en: Available now wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 各大播客平台现已上线。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《The Rest is History》。

sentences.en: It is the 30th of August, 1773.
sentences.zh: 现在是1773年8月30日。

sentences.en: Samuel Johnson and James Boswell have left Inverness.
sentences.zh: 塞缪尔·约翰逊和詹姆斯·博斯韦尔已经离开了因弗内斯。

sentences.en: They have left the world of stagecoaches and comfortable inns and civilised company.
sentences.zh: 他们离开了驿马车、舒适客栈和文明社交的世界。

sentences.en: And they are riding west into the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 他们正骑马向西驶入高地。

sentences.en: And their destination, Tom Loch Ness.
sentences.zh: 他们的目的地是，尼斯湖。

sentences.en: So Boswell writes about it.
sentences.zh: 于是博斯韦尔对此进行了记述。

sentences.en: Loch Ness and the road upon the side of it between birch trees with the hills above pleased us much.
sentences.zh: 尼斯湖及其侧畔、在桦树之间、山峦之下的道路让我们非常高兴。

sentences.en: The scene was as remote and agreeably wild as could be desired.
sentences.zh: 这里的景色比想象中还要偏远、宜人且荒凉。

sentences.en: Exciting.
sentences.zh: 令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So they don't spot the monster.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没有发现水怪。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Oh, disappointing.
sentences.zh: 哦，太让人失望了。

sentences.en: Nobody knows the monster exists.
sentences.zh: 没有人知道水怪的存在。

sentences.en: That's so disappointing.
sentences.zh: 太令人失望了。

sentences.en: I guess that's because the monster was invented in the 1930s by the Daily Mail, no?
sentences.zh: 我想那是因为水怪是《每日邮报》在20世纪30年代虚构出来的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you can hear our episode about that.
sentences.zh: 你可以收听我们关于这个话题的那期节目。

sentences.en: But, even though they don't spot the monster, Boswell does notice a very old woman standing outside a wretched little hovel, as Boswell puts it, made of earth.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管他们没有发现水怪，博斯韦尔确实注意到一个很老的老妇人站在一个简陋的小泥屋外面，正如博斯韦尔所说，那是用泥土建造的。

sentences.en: And it has a window.
sentences.zh: 而且它有一个窗户。

sentences.en: And the way the window is stopped is with a kind of a circle of turf.
sentences.zh: 堵住这个窗户的方法是用一圈草皮。

sentences.en: This for Boswell is amazing.
sentences.zh: 对博斯韦尔来说，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: And his kind of documentary maker instincts kick in.
sentences.zh: 他那种纪录片制作人的本能被激活了。

sentences.en: And he is filled with a desire to see Johnson step inside this hovel.
sentences.zh: 他心中充满了强烈的愿望，想看约翰逊走进这个简陋的小屋。

sentences.en: And so they all pile in and inside it they find a pot filled with goat meat bubbling over a peat fire.
sentences.zh: 于是他们一拥而入，在里面发现了一锅在泥煤火上咕嘟咕嘟煮着的山羊肉。

sentences.en: And Johnson, like Louis Theroux or someone, he's kind of interviewing this woman, even though she doesn't speak English.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊就像路易斯·塞瑟克斯或什么人一样，他正在采访这个女人，尽管她不会说英语。

sentences.en: She only speaks Gaelic or earth, as Johnson calls it.
sentences.zh: 她只会说盖尔语，或者用约翰逊的话说，是泥土般的语言。

sentences.en: So to quote Boswell, Mr. Johnson asked her where she slept.
sentences.zh: 所以，引用博斯韦尔的话，约翰逊先生问她睡在哪里。

sentences.en: I asked one of the guides, who asked her in earth, i.e. Gaelic.
sentences.zh: 我问了其中一个向导，向导用泥土的语言，也就是盖尔语问了她。

sentences.en: She spoke with a kind of high tone.
sentences.zh: 她说话带着一种高音调。

sentences.en: He told us she was afraid we wanted to go to bed to her.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我们，她害怕我们想和她上床。

sentences.en: This coquetry, or whatever it may be called, of so wretched a like being was truly ludicrous.
sentences.zh: 这种可怜之人的卖弄风情或无论怎么称呼的举动，实在是荒谬绝伦。

sentences.en: That's very ungallant by Boswell.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔这话说得真不够绅士。

sentences.en: He's being very mean about this woman just because she's old and maybe not as prepossessing as the people with him he consorts on Westminster Bridge.
sentences.zh: 他对这个女人非常尖酸刻薄，仅仅因为她老，而且可能不像他在威斯敏斯特桥上交往的那些伴侣那样迷人。

sentences.en: But maybe his reputation had gone before him.
sentences.zh: 但也许他的名声已经传到她前面了。

sentences.en: Yeah, she thinks, Jesus, Boswell's turned up.
sentences.zh: 是的，她心想，天哪，博斯韦尔来了。

sentences.en: I can see he's clutching a pint of wine.
sentences.zh: 我看到他手里正紧紧抓着一品脱葡萄酒。

sentences.en: I'm in for it now.
sentences.zh: 我这下可惨了。

sentences.en: So there is a lot of banter along this theme.
sentences.zh: 所以围绕这个主题有很多调侃。

sentences.en: Johnson makes exactly this point.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊恰恰就指出了这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think he's amused, but he's also embarrassed and he definitely doesn't want to hurt her delicacy.
sentences.zh: 我认为他觉得好笑，但他也感到尴尬，而且他绝对不想伤害她的敏感。

sentences.en: And so he refuses to go into the bedchamber.
sentences.zh: 所以他拒绝进入卧室。

sentences.en: Boswell inevitably does.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔难免还是进去了。

sentences.en: And he lights a piece of paper, goes in and inspects it.
sentences.zh: 他点燃了一张纸，进去视察了一番。

sentences.en: And he finds that it's all, you know, thrillingly basic.
sentences.zh: 他发现这一切，你知道的，简陋得令人兴奋。

sentences.en: It's everything that he'd been hoping for.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合他一直以来的期望。

sentences.en: They then sit down with the old woman and the old woman is incredibly hospitable.
sentences.zh: 然后他们和老妇人坐在一起，老妇人极其热情好客。

sentences.en: She gives them both a dram.
sentences.zh: 她请他们俩喝了一小杯酒。

sentences.en: And then she asks in return, do you have some snuff?
sentences.zh: 接着她反问，你们有鼻烟吗？

sentences.en: And they don't have any snuff, but they reach into their pockets and they both give her a sixpence.
sentences.zh: 他们没有鼻烟，但他们把手伸进口袋，各自给了她六便士。

sentences.en: And they're chatting away through the interpreter and she tells Johnson and Boswell that she is as happy as any woman in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他们通过翻译愉快地闲聊着，她告诉约翰逊和博斯韦尔，她和苏格兰的任何女人一样快乐。

sentences.en: And then when they go on their way, she sends them with prayers, which she offers up in Gaelic.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们上路时，她用盖尔语为他们作祈祷并送别他们。

sentences.en: And Boswell writes, Mr. Johnson was pleased at seeing for the first time such a state of human life.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔写道，约翰逊先生很高兴能第一次看到这样的人类生活状态。

sentences.en: So, oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那挺不错的。

sentences.en: This is what he's been looking for, basically, in the Highlands.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他在高地一直在寻找的东西。

sentences.en: So, they continue on their way following the line of Loch Ness southweSt.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们沿着尼斯湖向西南方向继续赶路。

sentences.en: And by nightfall, they have reached Fort Augustus, which is at the opposite end from Inverness, where they stay as guests of the governor.
sentences.zh: 到了夜幕降临时，他们到达了奥古斯都堡，它位于因弗内斯的另一端，他们在那里作为总督的客人住下。

sentences.en: And I have to say that when you read both Johnson and Boswell's account, particularly of this stretch along Loch Ness, there's quite a kind of Great Plains in the 1870s vibe.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，当你阅读约翰逊和博斯韦尔的记述，尤其是关于尼斯湖这一段时，有一种1870年代大平原的氛围。

sentences.en: You know, remote landscapes, forts, the sense of, you know, slight nervousness looking over your shoulder and everything.
sentences.zh: 你知道，偏远的风景，堡垒，那种环顾四周时略带紧张的感觉，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Reminds me of the stuff we did on stage about Scottish visitors going to the New World,
sentences.zh: 这让我想起我们在舞台上做过的关于苏格兰访客去新世界的短剧，

sentences.en: going to the United States in the sort of middle of the 19th century with dogs called peevish.
sentences.zh: 他们在19世纪中叶左右去美国，带着名叫“易怒”的狗。

sentences.en: Yes, get eaten by Native Americans.
sentences.zh: 是的，被美洲原住民吃掉。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 一点没错。

sentences.en: Anyway, so they go up into the mountains, don't they, the next day?
sentences.zh: 总之，他们第二天去了山区，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Johnson is really struck by the wildness.
sentences.zh: 而且约翰逊对那种野性印象深刻。

sentences.en: It's exactly what he expected.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合他的预期。

sentences.en: Everything basically is ticking.
sentences.zh: 基本上一切都符合要求。

sentences.en: It's ticking all his boxes, right?
sentences.zh: 完全戳中了他在意的所有点，对吧？

sentences.en: It's exactly as he hoped and dreamed it would be.
sentences.zh: 这完全是他所希望和梦想的样子。

sentences.en: And it's about this point that he starts thinking this would make a great book.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，他开始觉得这会是一本好书。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实这么想。

sentences.en: And he's still pondering this notion that he'd first had in St. Andrews,
sentences.zh: 他还在琢磨他最初在圣安德鲁斯产生的那个想法，

sentences.en: which is the contrast between all the industry and the bustle of the lowlands and the kind of the emptiness of northern Scotland.
sentences.zh: 也就是低地的工业和喧嚣与苏格兰北部那种空旷之间的对比。

sentences.en: And that evening, they've, you know, they've been travelling over wild, thinly inhabited upland regions.
sentences.zh: 那天傍晚，他们，你知道的，一直在荒凉、人烟稀少的高原地区旅行。

sentences.en: And they climb down and they arrive in Glen Morriston, which is a Glen where Bonnie Prince Charlie had taken refuge in a cave.
sentences.zh: 然后他们走下山，到达了格伦莫里斯顿，这是一个邦妮王子查理曾在山洞中避难的山谷。

sentences.en: And they look around them and they find that the Glen is almost empty.
sentences.zh: 他们环顾四周，发现这个山谷几乎空无一人。

sentences.en: It's kind of deserted of habitation.
sentences.zh: 几乎荒无人烟。

sentences.en: There is one place where they can stay.
sentences.zh: 只有一个地方他们可以住下。

sentences.en: And their landlord confirms to them, yes, that 70 men had gone out of the Glen to America.
sentences.zh: 他们的房东向他们证实，是的，有70个人从这个山谷去了美国。

sentences.en: And Johnson is really struck by this.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊对此感触颇深。

sentences.en: And he's thinking, you know, there is the sense here of some profound historic change.
sentences.zh: 他在想，你知道的，这里有一种深刻的历史变迁感。

sentences.en: And what is going on?
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: What explains it?
sentences.zh: 这该如何解释？

sentences.en: So he's kind of sitting there thinking it.
sentences.zh: 所以他就坐在那里思考着。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Boswell's emotions are a kind of typically Boswellian mix of kind of fastidious distaste for this awful place they're staying in.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，博斯韦尔的情绪是一种典型的博斯韦尔式混合体，既有对他们所住的这个糟糕地方的挑剔和厌恶，

sentences.en: But Boswell calls it a stye.
sentences.zh: 但博斯韦尔称之为猪圈。

sentences.en: But it's intermingled with a sense of romantic pride at how magnificent the scenery is and how splendid all the customs are.
sentences.zh: 不过其中又夹杂着一种浪漫的自豪感，赞叹风景是多么壮丽，风俗是多么奇妙。

sentences.en: So the fastidious distaste firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以先说那种挑剔的厌恶。

sentences.en: They're shown into their room.
sentences.zh: 他们被带进自己的房间。

sentences.en: I mean, it's awful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，太糟糕了。

sentences.en: It's obviously heaving with bedbugs.
sentences.zh: 很显然，里面到处都是臭虫。

sentences.en: Johnson doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊不在乎。

sentences.en: Johnson just kind of throws himself down and immediately falls asleep.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊只是往那一躺，倒头就睡着了。

sentences.en: Boswell lies on his kind of horrible mattress, stressing out about bedbugs.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔躺在他那种可怕的床垫上，为臭虫焦虑万分。

sentences.en: And he has this weird fancy that a spider was traveling from the Winscott towards my mouth.
sentences.zh: 他产生了一种奇怪的幻想，觉得有一只蜘蛛正从护壁板爬向他的嘴。

sentences.en: He finally falls asleep, wakes up early.
sentences.zh: 他终于睡着了，又醒得很早。

sentences.en: He's still very stressed.
sentences.zh: 他仍然非常焦虑。

sentences.en: And he began to imagine that the landlord being about to emigrate himself might murder us to get our money.
sentences.zh: 他开始想象，房东自己既然打算移民，会不会为了谋财而把我们杀了。

sentences.en: Johnson completely unperturbed.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊则完全镇定自若。

sentences.en: He's lying there with a colored handkerchief tied around his head.
sentences.zh: 他正躺在那里，头上系着一条彩色的手帕。

sentences.en: And Boswell actually has to kind of prod him to get him up.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔甚至不得不推醒他以让他起床。

sentences.en: They then go and have breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他们去吃早餐。

sentences.en: And at breakfast, Boswell's mood is immediately transformed by meeting a veteran of Bonnie Prince Charlie's army,
sentences.zh: 在早餐时，博斯韦尔的心情因为遇到了一位邦妮王子查理军队的老兵而瞬间转变，

sentences.en: a Highlander who had signed up with the prince when he'd first landed, gone down with him deep into England, come back to Culloden and escaped from Culloden.
sentences.zh: 那是一个高地人，在王子刚登陆时就加入了军队，跟着他深入英格兰腹地，回到了卡洛登并从卡洛登死里逃生。

sentences.en: And so he relates this whole story.
sentences.zh: 于是他讲述了这整个故事。

sentences.en: And Boswell, as he listens to it, repeatedly finds himself in tears and goes off on a kind of massive Scottish patriotism jag.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在聆听时，多次热泪盈眶，并陷入了一种强烈的苏格兰爱国主义狂热中。

sentences.en: So he writes the very Highland names or the sound of a bagpipe will stir my blood and fill me with a mixture of melancholy and respect for courage and pity for an unfortunate and superstitious regard for antiquity and inclination for war without thought.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，非常高地的名字或风笛的声音会激荡我的血液，让我充满忧郁与对勇气的敬意、对不幸的怜悯、对古代的迷信般敬意、对不计后果的战争的向往，

sentences.en: And in short, with a crowd of sensations.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，充斥着纷繁复杂的感受。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那挺浪漫的。

sentences.en: I mean, a crowd of sensations could be Boswell's motto.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，“纷繁复杂的感受”简直可以成为博斯韦尔的座右铭。

sentences.en: That's basically what he's all about.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他的全部写照。

sentences.en: So he's in a very romantic mood.
sentences.zh: 所以他当时处于一种非常浪漫的情绪中。

sentences.en: And a couple of days later, so by now it's the 2nd of September, they've reached the coast and they've boarded a boat and they're being rowed across to Skye.
sentences.zh: 几天后，到现在已经是9月2日了，他们到达了海岸，登上了一艘船，正被浆手载着横渡到斯凯岛。

sentences.en: And as they're being rowed, they pass the very point where Bonnie Prince Charlie had first landed on Scottish soil.
sentences.zh: 当他们划船前行时，他们经过了邦妮王子查理最初踏上苏格兰土地的那个地方。

sentences.en: And Boswell sits there and previously he said that his blood was stirred.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔坐在那里，之前他说过自己的血液被激荡了。

sentences.en: Now his mind is stirred.
sentences.zh: 现在他的心灵也被激荡了。

sentences.en: But basically, he's very, very stirred by all of this.
sentences.zh: 但总之，这一切让他非常非常激动。

sentences.en: But.
sentences.zh: 但是。

sentences.en: But, yeah.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的。

sentences.en: He's had a massive row with Johnson.
sentences.zh: 他和约翰逊大吵了一架。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？

sentences.en: He has.
sentences.zh: 确实吵了。

sentences.en: He had a huge.
sentences.zh: 他们大吵了一场。

sentences.en: I mean, they've been getting on so well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们之前一直相处得那么好。

sentences.en: But the day before they get taken in the boat to Skye, they've had a massive bust up.
sentences.zh: 但在他们乘船去斯凯岛的前一天，他们爆发了一场剧烈的争吵。

sentences.en: So they've been coming down a mountain.
sentences.zh: 当时他们正从山上下来。

sentences.en: Johnson is on this pony and he's so heavy that the poor pony stumbles.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊骑着一匹矮马，他太胖了以至于可怜的矮马都踉跄了。

sentences.en: So the guide reaches for the bridling.
sentences.zh: 于是向导伸手去抓缰绳。

sentences.en: He tries to calm down both Johnson and the pony.
sentences.zh: 他试图安抚约翰逊和矮马。

sentences.en: The pony is nervous.
sentences.zh: 矮马受到惊吓。

sentences.en: Johnson is kind of irate that the pony has collapsed under him.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊对矮马在他身下瘫软感到十分恼火。

sentences.en: And Johnson is kind of rumbling away.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊在一边气哼哼的。

sentences.en: And as he's doing this, the guide is trying to distract Johnson and cheer him up.
sentences.zh: 正当他这样时，向导试图转移约翰逊的注意力并让他高兴起来。

sentences.en: And he says, see such pretty goats.
sentences.zh: 他说，看那些漂亮的山羊。

sentences.en: Then he whistles and he makes them jump.
sentences.zh: 然后他吹了口哨，让它们跳跃起来。

sentences.en: And Boswell thinks this is hilarious.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔觉得这太滑稽了。

sentences.en: A common ignorant horse hirer imagining that he could divert, as one does a child, Mr. Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 一个普通而无知的租马人，居然想像哄小孩子一样去取悦塞缪尔·约翰逊先生。

sentences.en: And he can't stop laughing.
sentences.zh: 他笑得停不下来。

sentences.en: And Johnson has a massive, massive strop about it.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊为此大发雷霆。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Johnson's dignity has been completely undermined by this, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，因为约翰逊的尊严被这事彻底瓦解了，对吧？

sentences.en: He can't ride the pony.
sentences.zh: 他骑不了矮马。

sentences.en: The pony's collapsing.
sentences.zh: 矮马在垮掉。

sentences.en: They're going down the hill.
sentences.zh: 他们正在下山。

sentences.en: The bloke is treating him like he's a child and Boswell's laughing at him.
sentences.zh: 这家伙把他当小孩子一样对待，而博斯韦尔还在笑话他。

sentences.en: It's too much for Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这对约翰逊来说太过分了。

sentences.en: It's absolutely too much for Johnson.
sentences.zh: 对约翰逊来说绝对是奇耻大辱。

sentences.en: And one of the themes of this whole trip, which Boswell, you know, he'd known this, but it's repeatedly something that he's stumbling up against,
sentences.zh: 而这次旅行的整个主题之一，博斯韦尔（你知道的，他本来就知道这一点）却屡屡碰壁，

sentences.en: is that Johnson cannot bear to be made to look ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 那就是约翰逊最无法忍受自己看起来像个滑稽可笑的人。

sentences.en: And if he does, he almost always loses his temper.
sentences.zh: 如果真成这样，他几乎每次都会大发脾气。

sentences.en: And so he loses his temper now.
sentences.zh: 所以他现在就发脾气了。

sentences.en: And Boswell, after this kind of bust up, he rides ahead to kind of try and scope out their onward travel arrangements.
sentences.zh: 在这场争吵之后，博斯韦尔骑马先行，去为他们接下来的行程打探安排。

sentences.en: And Johnson takes this again as a personal insult.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊再次把这视为一种人身侮辱。

sentences.en: He sees it as Boswell thinks that he can't cope with riding as fast as he can.
sentences.zh: 他认为博斯韦尔觉得他无法跟上骑马的速度。

sentences.en: And when Boswell comes back, he says, do you know, I should have sooner thought of doing as you have done as picking a pocket.
sentences.zh: 当博斯韦尔回来时，他说，你知道吗，我宁愿去偷钱包，也不愿做你刚才做的事。

sentences.en: And it's only the following morning that they make up.
sentences.zh: 直到第二天早上他们才和好。

sentences.en: And again, there's this brilliant phrase, let's think no more on it.
sentences.zh: 而且这里又有一个绝妙的短语，别再想这事了。

sentences.en: Oh, I'm glad they made up anyway.
sentences.zh: 哦，不管怎样，我很高兴他们和好了。

sentences.en: They do make up.
sentences.zh: 他们确实和好了。

sentences.en: So they've got what they've got to look forward to.
sentences.zh: 所以他们还有值得期待的事情。

sentences.en: They haven't met any clan chiefs yet.
sentences.zh: 他们还没见过任何氏族酋长呢。

sentences.en: No, that's what they really want.
sentences.zh: 对，那才是他们真正想要的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's a clan chief coming.
sentences.zh: 所以有一位氏族酋长要来了。

sentences.en: And this is the chief of clan MacDonald of Sleet.
sentences.zh: 这就是斯利特的麦克唐纳氏族酋长。

sentences.en: So Sir Alexander MacDonald.
sentences.zh: 也就是亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士。

sentences.en: So tell me about him.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲他吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he's married to Elizabeth Boswell, who's a distant cousin of Boswell's.
sentences.zh: 好的，他娶了伊丽莎白·博斯韦尔，她是博斯韦尔的远亲。

sentences.en: So Boswell knows Sir Alexander MacDonald and had actually met with him in London.
sentences.zh: 所以博斯韦尔认识亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士，并且实际上在伦敦见过他。

sentences.en: And there Sir Alexander had issued a formal invitation because Boswell had said, oh, you know, we're coming to the Hebrides.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，因为博斯韦尔说过，哦，你知道的，我们要去赫布里底群岛，亚历山大爵士发出了正式的邀请。

sentences.en: So they're very excited about this because obviously they want to meet a real Hebridean clan chief.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对此非常兴奋，因为显然他们想见一位真正的赫布里底群岛部族酋长。

sentences.en: And they're approaching the southern tip of Skye and they're looking out and they see that Sir Alexander has come down to the sea's edge to welcome them.
sentences.zh: 当他们接近斯凯岛的南端并向外眺望时，他们看到亚历山大爵士已经来到水边迎接他们。

sentences.en: And what's even better, he is in full tartan.
sentences.zh: 而且更棒的是，他身穿全套格子呢呢裙。

sentences.en: And this is massively exciting because tartan is actually, strictly speaking, illegal.
sentences.zh: 这让人无比兴奋，因为严格来说，格子呢其实是违法的。

sentences.en: In the wake of Culloden, it had been prescribed for everyone except for Highlanders serving with the British army.
sentences.zh: 卡洛登之役后，除了在英国军队服役的高地人外，所有人均被禁止穿着格子呢。

sentences.en: And so the fact that Sir Alexander MacDonald has turned up in the traditional Highland dress, this portends tremendous, tremendous entertainment.
sentences.zh: 因此，亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士竟然穿着传统的高地服饰露面，这预示着将有极好极好的消遣。

sentences.en: What's even better is that Lady MacDonald, who's very beautiful, she is standing at the top of the bank and she is making, to quote Boswell, a kind of jumping for joy.
sentences.zh: 更妙的是，非常漂亮的麦克唐纳夫人正站在堤岸顶上，用博斯韦尔的话说，她表现得像是在欢呼雀跃。

sentences.en: So everything seems set for a taste of traditional Hebridean hospitality.
sentences.zh: 因此，一切似乎都准备就绪，可以体验传统的赫布里底群岛好客之道了。

sentences.en: Except that this is not what they get.
sentences.zh: 奈何他们得到的并不是这回事。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，并没有。

sentences.en: Sir Alexander turns out to be an absolutely terrible hoSt.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大爵士结果是个绝对糟糕的主人。

sentences.en: He's kind of mean, he's really boring and he's boorish.
sentences.zh: 他有点小气，真的很无聊而且很粗俗。

sentences.en: And there are no clansmen.
sentences.zh: 而且这里没有族人。

sentences.en: There are no claymores, kind of no outlander vibes in any way.
sentences.zh: 没有阔剑，完全没有那种异乡客的风情。

sentences.en: The dinner is a shocker.
sentences.zh: 晚餐糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: It's kind of undercooked.
sentences.zh: 有点没熟透。

sentences.en: It's boring.
sentences.zh: 令人乏味。

sentences.en: Sir Alexander hasn't brought his chef with him to the island.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大爵士没有把他的厨师带到岛上来。

sentences.en: The punch, there's almost no alcohol in the punch at all.
sentences.zh: 潘趣酒里几乎一点酒精都没有。

sentences.en: Oh, that's the lowest thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，这可真是太逊了。

sentences.en: That's poor.
sentences.zh: 真够差劲的。

sentences.en: And Lady MacDonald, whom Boswell remembered as being absolutely enchanting.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔记忆中无比迷人的麦克唐纳夫人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It seems, I mean, Johnson, Johnson says she seems cut out of a cabbage.
sentences.zh: 看来，我是说，约翰逊，约翰逊说她看起来就像是用卷心菜雕出来的。

sentences.en: This woman would sink a 90-gun ship.
sentences.zh: 这个女人能让一艘90门大炮的战舰沉没。

sentences.en: She is so dull and heavy.
sentences.zh: 她是如此沉闷而笨重。

sentences.en: Oh, Jesus.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That's even more disappointing than the punch.
sentences.zh: 这甚至比潘趣酒还要令人失望。

sentences.en: God, this is ticking none of my boxes.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这完全不符合我的任何期待。

sentences.en: So that's very dispiriting.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And Boswell is mortified, kind of on his own behalf, but also on behalf of Scotland.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔感到十分难堪，既是为他自己，也是替苏格兰感到丢脸。

sentences.en: This is exactly, he doesn't want Johnson seeing, you know, it's not what he wants at all.
sentences.zh: 这正是他不想让约翰逊看到的，你知道的，这根本不是他想要的。

sentences.en: Sir Alexander MacDonald has let Scotland down.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士让苏格兰失望了。

sentences.en: So he has a blazing row with Sir Alexander.
sentences.zh: 于是他和亚历山大爵士大吵了一架。

sentences.en: Get a better wife, for God's sake.
sentences.zh: 看在上帝的份上，找个好点儿的妻子吧。

sentences.en: Boswell wants to leave that night.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔当晚就想离开。

sentences.en: Johnson says, no, we can't.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊说，不行，我们不能走。

sentences.en: That would be rude.
sentences.zh: 那太失礼了。

sentences.en: So they stay there for four days.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在那里呆了四天。

sentences.en: They head off to go and stay with these other people who've invited them.
sentences.zh: 他们动身去拜访其他邀请过他们的人。

sentences.en: And from there, they're going to make a crossing to the nearby island of Arrasi.
sentences.zh: 从那里出发，他们将横渡海峡前往附近的拉赛岛。

sentences.en: And they kind of arrive, they're ready to get in the boat, but then that kind of massive storm blows up and they can't make the crossing.
sentences.zh: 他们差不多到了，准备上船，但接着就刮起了那样一场大风暴，他们无法渡海了。

sentences.en: So this is very disappointing as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是非常令人失望的。

sentences.en: And Johnson, sensing that Boswell is bored, starts to entertain him with an impersonation of Lady MacDonald, leaning forward with a hand on each cheek and her mouth open.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊察觉到博斯韦尔很无聊，便开始模仿麦克唐纳夫人来取乐：她身体前倾，双手托着双颊，嘴巴张开。

sentences.en: And Boswell, unlike Lord Affleck, his father, is a big fan of impersonations.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔不像他的父亲奥斯利勋爵，他非常喜欢模仿秀。

sentences.en: And he thinks that Johnson has absolutely nailed this impersonation.
sentences.zh: 他认为约翰逊把这个模仿得惟妙惟肖。

sentences.en: And he writes, to see such a beauty represented by Mr. Johnson was excessively high.
sentences.zh: 他写道，看到这样一位美人被约翰逊先生演绎出来，实在是妙不可趣。

sentences.en: But there are only so many impersonations of Lady MacDonald that can be done over the course of two days.
sentences.zh: 但在短短两天里，模仿麦克唐纳夫人的次数毕竟是有限的。

sentences.en: And so by the time the storm finally subsides, they are so ready to cross to Arrasi.
sentences.zh: 因此，当风暴终于平息时，他们是如此渴望渡海前往拉赛岛。

sentences.en: But there are only so many times that Johnson can do an impersonation of Lady MacDonald.
sentences.zh: 但约翰逊模仿麦克唐纳夫人的次数也是有限的。

sentences.en: And so they're stuck there for two days.
sentences.zh: 所以他们被困在那里两整天。

sentences.en: And Boswell is just, you know, so depressed.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔简直是，你知道的，沮丧透顶。

sentences.en: Have all Johnson's criticisms of Scotland, you know, have they been based in fact?
sentences.zh: 难道约翰逊对苏格兰的所有批评，你知道的，都是基于事实吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is he right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他是对的吗？

sentences.en: Is Scotland actually a terrible place?
sentences.zh: 苏格兰其实是个糟糕的地方吗？

sentences.en: So actually Johnson's perspective is slightly different though, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 不过其实约翰逊的视角稍微有些不同，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because he's basically struck by how much has changed in Scotland in recent years.
sentences.zh: 因为他基本上对近年来苏格兰发生の巨大变化感到震惊。

sentences.en: He's almost quite mournful and quite melancholy about it.
sentences.zh: 他对此几乎感到十分感伤和忧郁。

sentences.en: He says basically, clearly there was some romantic, you know, mist-shrouded, beautiful Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说，很明显，曾经存在过某种浪漫的、云雾缭绕的美丽苏格兰。

sentences.en: But it has been destroyed or it's being loSt.
sentences.zh: 但它已经被摧毁了，或者正在消逝。

sentences.en: And that's what really is on his mind.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正萦绕在他心头的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he writes in his book, we came there too late to see what we expected.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以他在书中写道，我们到那儿太晚了，未能见到我们所期望的景象。

sentences.en: A people of peculiar appearance and a system of antiquated life.
sentences.zh: 一群外表奇特的人和一套陈旧古老的生活体系。

sentences.en: So Boswell is blaming Sir Alexander for their poor reception.
sentences.zh: 所以博斯韦尔把他们受到的冷遇怪罪于亚历山大爵士。

sentences.en: And I think that's reasonable enough.
sentences.zh: 我想这倒也合情合理。

sentences.en: But I think Johnson is seeing it in a slightly deeper, kind of profounder historical context.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得约翰逊是从一个稍微更深层、更具深度的历史背景来看待这件事的。
