sentences.en: And I think he feels essentially that they've come there too late and that recent history, you know, its effects have been remorseless.
sentences.zh: 我想他基本上觉得他们到得太晚了，而且近代历史，你知道的，其影响是冷酷无情的。

sentences.en: There hasn't really been any resisting it.
sentences.zh: 根本没有什么抵抗的余地。

sentences.en: Because Scotland has joined with England in the Union and as a result has become richer.
sentences.zh: 因为苏格兰与英格兰合并加入了联邦，因此变得更加富裕。

sentences.en: You know, it's joined this enormous single market.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它加入了这个庞大的单一市场。

sentences.en: It's become more prosperous.
sentences.zh: 它变得更加繁荣了。

sentences.en: It's become a commercial nation, a polite and commercial nation.
sentences.zh: 它变成了一个商业国家，一个文雅而商业化的国家。

sentences.en: But only in the lowlands.
sentences.zh: 但仅限于低地地区。

sentences.en: And Johnson feels that the wealthier the lowlands have grown, the less prepared the elites of Edinburgh and Glasgow have been to put up with the autonomy of the clans.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊觉得，低地地区越富有，爱丁堡和格拉斯哥的精英阶层就越无法容忍部族的自治。

sentences.en: And the law had begun to disarm the clans.
sentences.zh: 法律已经开始解除部族的武装。

sentences.en: So Johnson writes,
sentences.zh: 因此约翰逊写道，

sentences.en: the chief has lost his formidable retinue and the Highlander walks his heath unarmed and defenceless with the peaceable submission of a French peasant or English cottager.
sentences.zh: 酋长已经失去了他那威风凛凛的随从，高地人赤手空拳、毫无防备地走在他们的荒原上，带着法兰西农民或英格兰村夫般温顺的服从。

sentences.en: And this is something obviously that has struck Johnson only on their tour because, remember, he had brought his pistols with him.
sentences.zh: 这显然是约翰逊在他们的旅行中才突然意识到的事情，因为记住，他是随身带了手枪的。

sentences.en: But now he finds there aren't any pistols.
sentences.zh: 但现在他发现根本没有手枪了。

sentences.en: There aren't any claymores.
sentences.zh: 也没有阔剑了。

sentences.en: You know, the Highlanders have have no weapons whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，高地人没有任何武器可言。

sentences.en: And this is partly because Scottish laws have disarmed them, but it's also British state repression following the Battle of Culloden when, you know,
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为苏格兰法律解除了他们的武装，但这也是卡洛登战役后英国国家镇压的结果，当时，你知道的，

sentences.en: the Hanoverian regime had received this terrible shock.
sentences.zh: 汉诺威政权受到了可怕的惊吓。

sentences.en: And it's in the wake of that that the Tartan had been banned and carrying weapons and all kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 正是在那之后，格子呢被禁了，携带武器以及诸如此类的事情也被禁了。

sentences.en: And Johnson writes,
sentences.zh: 约翰逊写道，

sentences.en: their pride had been crushed by the heavy hand of a vindictive conqueror and that chiefs had degenerated from patriarchal rulers to rapacious landlords and that many of the chiefs,
sentences.zh: 他们的傲骨已被一个好胜征服者的铁腕所摧毁，酋长们已经从宗法式的统治者堕落为贪婪的房东，许多酋长

sentences.en: rather than stay in their ancestral strongholds, surrounded by their clansmen, that most of them have migrated southwards to the lowlands, to Glasgow, to Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 宁愿不在祖传的堡垒里由部族成员簇拥着居住，而是大部分都向南迁移到了低地，去了格拉斯哥，去了爱丁堡。

sentences.en: Some of them have even gone to London and it doesn't surprise Johnson at all to learn that Sir Alexander MacDonald had been educated at Eton.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人甚至去了伦敦，当约翰逊得知亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士曾就读于伊顿公学时，他一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: So, yeah, they're losing their Scottishness.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他们正在失去苏格兰特色。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, certainly they're losing their status as a, you know, a Hebridean clan chief.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，他们确实在失去作为赫布里底群岛部族酋长的地位。

sentences.en: The clan chiefs are all going to Eton and the clansmen, rather than kind of choose to moulder in glens or on the Isles or whatever, are increasingly leaving for America,
sentences.zh: 部族酋长们全都去了伊顿公学，而族人们与其选择在峡谷或岛屿上或什么地方腐朽老去，不如越来越多地离开前往美洲，

sentences.en: either to fight for the British army there or to set up as colonists.
sentences.zh: 要么去那里为英格兰军队作战，要么去建立殖民地。

sentences.en: And Johnson feels that it's not really the union that's brought this about, that it's not even Culloden that has doomed them,
sentences.zh: 约翰逊觉得，导致这一切的并非真的是联邦，甚至不是卡洛登战役注定了他们的命运，

sentences.en: that it is actually just the kind of the inexorable way of things, that this is how a commercialising nation, a prospering nation, that there are victiMs.
sentences.zh: 实际上这只是事物不可阻挡的发展规律，一个走向商业化、繁荣的国家就是这样，总会有牺牲品。

sentences.en: Doesn't it go back to your parallel that you made earlier on with the Plains Indians and visitors to the Great Plains,
sentences.zh: 这难道不契合你之前做出的那个类比吗，就是关于平原印第安人和大平原访客的类比，

sentences.en: that you could conceivably visit the Great Plains in the late 19th century and you'd take your pistols thinking, there's part of you that thinks, gosh,
sentences.zh: 你可以想象自己在19世纪后期访问大平原，你会随身携带手枪，心里会想，你会有一部分心思想，天哪，

sentences.en: are we going to be taken prisoner by the Sioux or something?
sentences.zh: 我们会不会被苏族人或其他什么人俘虏呢？

sentences.en: And you get there and it's all gone and it's all changed and it's partly repression and it's partly the process of, you know,
sentences.zh: 等你到了那里，发现一切都消失了，一切都变了，部分原因是镇压，部分原因是

sentences.en: capitalism and industrialisation and urbanisation and all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 资本主义、工业化、城市化以及所有这些事情的发展进程。

sentences.en: And this is a preview of that, no?
sentences.zh: 而这正是那事的预演，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah,
sentences.zh: 是的，

sentences.en: and I think what Johnson says about the process of immiseration that are essentially destroying the traditions of the Highlands could equally be applied to the Plains Indians.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为约翰逊对那些基本上在摧毁高地传统的 impoverishment（贫困化）进程的看法，同样适用于平原印第安人。

sentences.en: So he writes, misery is caused for the most part not by a heavy crush of disaster, but by the corrosion of less visible evils, which canker enjoyment and undermine security.
sentences.zh: 所以他写道，苦难的产生在很大程度上并非由于灾难的重压，而是由于那些不那么显眼的恶习的侵蚀，它们蚕食了快乐并破坏了安全感。

sentences.en: The visit of an invader is necessarily rare, but domestic animosities allow no cessation.
sentences.zh: 入侵者的造访必然是罕见的，但内心的敌意却从不间断。

sentences.en: And so this is the judgment that he delivers in his book on the Western Islands, you know, and it's a kind of sombre one, it's a profound one.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他在关于西方群岛的书中所作出的评价，你知道的，这是一种沉郁的评价，一种深刻的评价。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that's true more generally.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为这在更广泛的意义上也是真实的。

sentences.en: I mean, you could apply it perhaps to life in Western democracies at the moment if you wanted to.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你愿意的话，也许可以把它应用到当今西方民主国家的生活中去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there are people in Scotland when this book comes out who say, well, this is just because Johnson hates Scotland.
sentences.zh: 当这本书出版时，苏格兰有些人说，这只是因为约翰逊讨厌苏格兰。

sentences.en: I don't think this is true.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是真的。

sentences.en: I don't think actually I think Johnson has a wonderful time in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 我不认为——实际上我认为约翰逊在苏格兰过得很愉快。

sentences.en: He's writing as a man who has an instinctive sympathy for the underdog,
sentences.zh: 他写作时是一个对弱势群体有着本能同情的人，

sentences.en: but he is also writing as someone who in the course of his travels does actually see enough of the traditional Highland ways to feel very, very wistful for their decline.
sentences.zh: 但他在旅行过程中也确实亲眼目睹了足够多的传统高地生活方式，以至于对它们的衰落感到非常非常的留恋。

sentences.en: And what he sees, he enjoys so much that he from this point on will always refer to his travels in the Western Isles as the pleasantest part of my life.
sentences.zh: 他所看到的一切是如此令他享受，以至于从这时起，他总是将自己在西部群岛的旅行称为我一生中最快乐的时光。

sentences.en: Oh, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太好了。

sentences.en: So Boswell actually needn't have worried.
sentences.zh: 所以博斯韦尔其实完全不必担心。

sentences.en: Johnson isn't having a bad time.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊过得并不糟糕。

sentences.en: He hadn't been put off by Sir Alexander MacDonald sticking his fork into a liver pudding while his guests were kept standing.
sentences.zh: 他并没有因为亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士在客人站着的时候把叉子插进肝布丁里而感到扫兴。

sentences.en: He hasn't been put off by the storMs.
sentences.zh: 他也没有被风暴所吓退。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, it's Western Scotland.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，那是苏格兰西部。

sentences.en: He's Johnson's expecting storMs.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊本来就料到会有风暴。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the two months in the Hebrides that follow this kind of slightly unfortunate introduction to Sky, they are a triumph.
sentences.zh: 紧随斯凯岛这段略显不幸的初访之后的赫布里底群岛两个月之旅，简直是一场大获成功。

sentences.en: So Racy, when they finally reach it, proves an absolute ball.
sentences.zh: 因此，当他们最终抵达拉赛岛时，证明这是一场绝对的狂欢。

sentences.en: There's everything that they'd been hoping for from Sir Alexander MacDonald.
sentences.zh: 这里有一切他们对亚历山大·麦克唐纳爵士抱有的期待。

sentences.en: There's fiddling, there's dancing.
sentences.zh: 有拉小提琴的，有跳舞的。

sentences.en: And even though Johnson sits out the reels, he's absolutely in his element.
sentences.zh: 尽管约翰逊没有参与里尔舞，但他完全处于自己最舒适的状态。

sentences.en: And Boswell wrote in great relief, Mr. Johnson was in fine spirits.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔如释重负地写道，约翰逊先生情绪高昂。

sentences.en: He said, this is truly the patriarchal life.
sentences.zh: 他说，这真是有如宗法般的生活。

sentences.en: This is what we came to find.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们远道而来寻找的。

sentences.en: Oh, they come back to Sky and they travel to Kingsborough and there they meet the ultimate in living Jacobite history.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们回到斯凯岛，前往金斯伯在那里他们遇到了活生生的詹姆斯党历史的巅峰。

sentences.en: And this is Flora MacDonald, the woman who had saved Bonnie Prince Charlie.
sentences.zh: 这就是弗洛拉·麦克唐纳，那个拯救了查理王子的人。

sentences.en: And she had escorted the wanderer, as Boswell calls him, disguised as her Irish maid, Betty Burke.
sentences.zh: 正如博斯韦尔所称的那样，她曾护送这位流亡者，当时他伪装成她的爱尔兰女佣贝蒂·伯克。

sentences.en: And it has to be said that, according to Flora MacDonald, he didn't make a very convincing Irish maid.
sentences.zh: 必须指出的是，据弗洛拉·麦克唐纳所说，他装扮的爱尔兰女佣并不怎么逼真。

sentences.en: She'd brought him from the Outer Hebrides to Sky.
sentences.zh: 她把他从外赫布里底群岛带到了斯凯岛。

sentences.en: And from Sky, Bonnie Prince Charlie had been taken onwards to the mainland again and put on a ship and taken back to France.
sentences.zh: 从斯凯岛出发，查理王子又被带到大陆，送上一艘船被带回了法国。

sentences.en: And again, Boswell, the documentary director, to see Mr. Samuel Johnson salute Miss Flora MacDonald was a wonderful romantic scene to me.
sentences.zh: 同样的，作为纪录片导演的博斯韦尔写道，看到萨缪尔·约翰逊先生向弗洛拉·麦克唐纳小姐致敬，对我来说是一个无比浪漫的场景。

sentences.en: And what's even more romantic is that they stay in Flora MacDonald's house and Johnson sleeps in the very bed that Bonnie Prince Charlie had slept in.
sentences.zh: 更浪漫的是，他们住在弗洛拉·麦克唐纳的房子里，约翰逊睡的正是查理王子睡过的那张床。

sentences.en: So if you're a Bonnie Prince Charlie tourist, I mean, you know, this is incredible.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是个查理王子的游客，我的意思是，你知道的，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're an old Tory like Samuel Johnson with Jacobite sympathies, this must be absolutely fantastic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你是一个像萨缪尔·约翰逊那样带有詹姆斯党同情心的老派保守党人，这绝对是棒极了。

sentences.en: Absolute heaven.
sentences.zh: 简直是人间天堂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he really is having a brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实度过了一段精彩绝伦的时光。

sentences.en: And I think the final highlight for Johnson is perhaps the most moving of all.
sentences.zh: 我想约翰逊此行的最后一个高潮也许是最让人感动的。

sentences.en: And they say they go to Mull and then they take a crossing, a very short crossing to Iona, which is a holy island for the Scots.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们去了马尔岛，然后乘船渡海，一次非常短的航行就到了爱奥那岛，对苏格兰人来说这是一座神圣的岛屿。

sentences.en: And indeed, I think for any British Christian, St. Columba, the Irish monk, had founded a monastery there back in 563, commemorated as the great cradle of Scottish Christianity.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我认为对任何英国基督徒来说也是如此，爱尔兰僧侣圣高隆早在563年就在那里建立了一座修道院，这里被纪念为苏格兰基督教的伟大摇篮。

sentences.en: And Johnson feels an immense surge of emotion visiting it.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊在参观时感到一股排山倒海般的情感涌上心头。

sentences.en: And he wrote about it in a very, very famous line,
sentences.zh: 他在一首非常非常著名的诗句中写道，

sentences.en: that man is little to be envied whose patriotism would not gain force upon the plain of Marathon or whose piety would not grow warmer among the ruins of Iona.
sentences.zh: 若有人之爱国情怀在马拉松平原上不能激发，或其虔诚信仰在爱奥那岛的废墟中不能升华，此人实乃无可救药。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: So for Boswell, you describe him as a documentary maker.
sentences.zh: 所以对于博斯韦尔，你把他描述为一个纪录片制作人。

sentences.en: I mean, he's got all the shots he wanted.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他拍到了他想要的所有镜头。

sentences.en: He's got Johnson in Bonnie Prince Charlie's bed.
sentences.zh: 他拍到了约翰逊睡在小王子查理的床上的画面。

sentences.en: He's got Johnson looking, you know, melancholy and thoughtful and stirred with a religious feeling in the ruins of Iona.
sentences.zh: 他拍到了约翰逊在爱奥那岛的废墟中，那种流露出忧郁、沉思以及宗教情怀的神情。

sentences.en: I mean, he's made a tremendous film.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他拍出了一部极了不起的电影。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so all their kind of, you know, memories of rows about ponies and so on have ended up pretty much forgotten.
sentences.zh: 所以他们诸如关于小马争吵之类的种种记忆，基本上都被遗忘了。

sentences.en: And in fact, there are only two episodes during the whole tour around the Hebrides, which it would subsequently cause Boswell pain to recall.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在环赫布里底群岛的整个旅程中，只有两段插曲是后来让博斯韦尔回想起来觉得痛苦的。

sentences.en: And the first of these had occurred on the 16th of September.
sentences.zh: 其中第一段发生在9月16日。

sentences.en: Johnson had a cold, but was otherwise in fine form.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊有点感冒，但除此之外状态极佳。

sentences.en: And he's, you know, talking away about a whole host of things.
sentences.zh: 而且他，你知道的，滔滔不绝地谈论着一大堆事情。

sentences.en: And he suddenly, it seems to Boswell, goes off on a mad one.
sentences.zh: 然后在博斯韦尔看来，他突然就变得有点疯狂了。

sentences.en: Johnson says, I have often thought that if I kept a seraglio, so a harem, the ladies should all wear linen gowns or cotton.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊说：“我常常想，如果我养一个后宫，那么女士们都应该穿着亚麻长裙或棉布长裙。”

sentences.en: I mean, stuffs made of vegetable substances.
sentences.zh: 我是说，用植物纤维制作的织物。

sentences.en: And he's saying this because they've been talking about how linen is is kind of vastly preferable to anything with animal substances.
sentences.zh: 他这么说是，因为他们一直在讨论亚麻在各方面是如何远胜于任何动物材质的东西。

sentences.en: But it is a slightly unexpected left field.
sentences.zh: 但这算是一个有点出其不意的离奇话题。

sentences.en: Sally.
sentences.zh: 莎莉。

sentences.en: And the fact that he said, I have often thought that if I kept a harem, I mean, Boswell finds this so unexpected that he bursts out laughing.
sentences.zh: 鉴于他说过“我常常想，如果我养一个后宫”，博斯韦尔觉得这太出人意料了，以至于哈哈大笑起来。

sentences.en: Johnson doesn't like that.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Johnson doesn't like this because he feels that he is now an object of ridicule.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊不喜欢这样，因为他觉得自己现在成了被嘲笑的对象。

sentences.en: And in the kind of the published version of his journals, Boswell says he was too proud to submit, even for a moment,
sentences.zh: 在出版的日记版本中，博斯韦尔说他“傲骨凛凛，甚至连片刻都不肯屈服”，

sentences.en: to be the object of ridicule and instantly retaliated with keen, sarcastic wit and a variety of degrading images.
sentences.zh: 不愿成为被嘲笑的对象，并立刻用尖锐、讽刺的机智以及各种贬损的意象进行了反击。

sentences.en: And Boswell doesn't specify what these degrading images are in the book.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在书中没有明确说明这些贬损的意象是什么。

sentences.en: But in his journal, he had done.
sentences.zh: 但在他的日记里，他写了。

sentences.en: And essentially what Johnson had done was to say, oh, well, if I had a harem, you would be the eunuch.
sentences.zh: 基本上，约翰逊所做的是说，哦，好吧，如果我有一个后宫，你就会当那个太监。

sentences.en: And there are some quite deep waters here, I feel, because, of course, Boswell had wanted to keep a harem for himself.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这里面水挺深的，因为当然了，博斯韦尔自己就曾想过要养一个后宫。

sentences.en: He talked about that with Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 他曾和卢梭谈论过这件事。

sentences.en: And the idea of being a eunuch to Johnson, I mean, it just seems so wrong.
sentences.zh: 而成为约翰逊的太监这个想法，我是说，这听起来太离谱了。

sentences.en: It hits him on various levels because Boswell is so priapic that for him to be a eunuch, to be unmanned in this way, is an insult to his masculinity.
sentences.zh: 这在各个层面都打击了他，因为博斯韦尔性欲极强，对他来说，当太监、以这种方式被剥夺男儿身，是对他男子气概的侮辱。

sentences.en: But also, he kind of is Johnson's eunuch already.
sentences.zh: 但同时，某种程度上他也已经是约翰逊的“太监”了。

sentences.en: Well, he's the attendant, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是那个随从，对吧？

sentences.en: He's the subordinate figure.
sentences.zh: 他是那个处于从属地位的人物。

sentences.en: Yes, he's Johnson's super fan.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是约翰逊的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think there's a lot going on there.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得这其中有很多深意。

sentences.en: And so Boswell writes, I would gladly expunge from my mind every trace of this severe retort.
sentences.zh: 因此博斯韦尔写道：“我愿欣然从我脑海中抹去这一严厉反击的每一丝痕迹。”

sentences.en: And you can see why.
sentences.zh: 你能理解为什么。

sentences.en: It's clearly striking him on all kinds of levels.
sentences.zh: 这显然在各个层面上都打击了他。

sentences.en: Then there is a second episode, which is very famous.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二段插曲，非常有名。

sentences.en: And again, Boswell could not bring himself to relate it in full.
sentences.zh: 同样，博斯韦尔无法说服自己完整地叙述它。

sentences.en: And it takes place at the very end of their journey.
sentences.zh: 它发生在他们旅程的最后阶段。

sentences.en: They've come back from the Hebrides.
sentences.zh: 他们从赫布里底群岛回来了。

sentences.en: They're heading down to Edinburgh.
sentences.zh: 他们正朝着爱丁堡前进。

sentences.en: But before they reach Edinburgh, they head southwards to the one place in Scotland that Johnson had always said he'd wanted to see and which Boswell had always longed to show him.
sentences.zh: 但在到达爱丁堡之前，他们向南前往苏格兰的一个地方——约翰逊一直说他想看，而博斯韦尔也一直渴望带他去看看的地方。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is the ancestral seat of the Boswells, Affleck.
sentences.zh: 那当然就是博斯韦尔家族的祖居地，奥克兰。

sentences.en: That's risky.
sentences.zh: 这很冒险。

sentences.en: It is risky.
sentences.zh: 确实很冒险。

sentences.en: Because his father, his father is, what is he?
sentences.zh: 因为他的父亲，他的父亲是，他是什么人？

sentences.en: He's a Whig.
sentences.zh: 他是个辉格党人。

sentences.en: He's a Presbyterian.
sentences.zh: 他是个长老会信徒。

sentences.en: He's a Hanoverian.
sentences.zh: 他是个汉诺威王朝支持者。

sentences.en: He's got no sense of fun or humour.
sentences.zh: 他一点乐趣或幽默感都没有。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't see him getting on with Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我看不出他能和塞缪尔·约翰逊合得来。

sentences.en: I mean, he has got a sense of humour, but it's very sharp and bitter and kind of piercing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他确实有幽默感，但非常尖刻、苦涩且带有某种穿透力。

sentences.en: It's not jolly.
sentences.zh: 那可不是什么好玩的幽默。

sentences.en: And Boswell knows this.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔深知这一点。

sentences.en: And so he says, if Lord Affleck had not invited Johnson, I would not have taken him there.
sentences.zh: 所以他说：“如果奥克兰勋爵没有邀请约翰逊，我是不会带他去的。”

sentences.en: Because, you know, he'd be fearing the worst, you know, worried about fireworks.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，他会做最坏的打算，担心会擦枪走火。

sentences.en: But Lord Affleck had insisted.
sentences.zh: 但奥克兰勋爵坚持要他们去。

sentences.en: And so Boswell and Johnson had duly arrived at Affleck on the 2nd of November.
sentences.zh: 于是博斯韦尔和约翰逊于11月2日如期抵达了奥克兰。

sentences.en: And to begin with, everything goes well.
sentences.zh: 起初，一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: Both men behave themselves.
sentences.zh: 两个人都规规矩矩的。

sentences.en: Johnson has a lovely time being led up by Boswell to inspect the ruins of the old castle on the, you know, on the gorge above the rivers.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊过得很愉快，在博斯韦尔的带领下去考察了河流上方峡谷中的古城堡废墟。

sentences.en: And the days pass and things seem to be perfectly amiable between Lord Affleck and Johnson.
sentences.zh: 日子一天天过去，奥克兰勋爵和约翰逊之间似乎相处得十分融洽。

sentences.en: But then on the 6th of November, disaster.
sentences.zh: 但随后在11月6日，灾难降临了。

sentences.en: So Lord Affleck has a collection of medals and he keeps them in the library in his great classical house that he's just had built.
sentences.zh: 原来奥克兰勋爵收藏了一套勋章，他把它们保存在他刚刚建好的宏伟古典风格宅邸的书房里。

sentences.en: And he pulls them out and he shows them to Johnson.
sentences.zh: 他把它们拿出来展示给约翰逊看。

sentences.en: When Oliver Cromwell's coin unfortunately introduced Charles I and Toryism.
sentences.zh: 当时奥利弗·克伦威尔的硬币不幸引出了查理一世和托利党主义。

sentences.en: It's like when we do a thing and we end up with George Hours.
sentences.zh: 就像我们做一件事，最后却弄出了“乔治·奥尔”一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The publisher and historian.
sentences.zh: 出版商兼历史学家。

sentences.en: Couple loft.
sentences.zh: 库普·洛夫特。

sentences.en: And we accidentally praise Oliver Cromwell and he goes ballistic and starts shouting about Charles I.
sentences.zh: 我们不小心称赞了奥利弗·克伦威尔，然后他就勃然大怒，开始大谈查理一世。

sentences.en: This is what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: This is the essence of Toryism.
sentences.zh: 这就是托利党主义的精髓。

sentences.en: The belief that Charles I should not have had his head chopped off.
sentences.zh: 坚信查理一世本不该被砍头。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lord Affleck is much more impressed by the execution and says that it reminds kings that they have vertebrae in their necks.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰勋爵对这场处决印象深刻得多，并说这提醒了国王们，他们的脖子上长着脊椎骨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Johnson just explodes and the row goes on and on.
sentences.zh: 然后约翰逊直接勃然大怒，争吵没完没了。

sentences.en: And Boswell, he can't avoid mentioning it in his book because it's really quite famous.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在书中无法避而不谈此事，因为它实在太出名了。

sentences.en: The news of it leaks out.
sentences.zh: 这消息不胫而走。

sentences.en: But he refuses to go into details.
sentences.zh: 但他拒绝透露细节。

sentences.en: It would certainly be very unbecoming in me to exhibit my honoured father and my respected friend as intellectual gladiators for the entertainment of the public.
sentences.zh: “把备受尊敬的父亲和尊崇的朋友展示为供公众娱乐的智力角斗士，这对我来说无疑是极不体面的。”

sentences.en: And you slightly feel reading that.
sentences.zh: 读到这里，你隐隐会有一种感觉。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, nothing has stopped you doing exactly that before.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，以前没有什么能阻止你做类似的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, Boswell only has to hear a conversation and he's transcribing it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，博斯韦尔只要听到一段对话，就会把它记录下来。

sentences.en: But not when they've gone head to head.
sentences.zh: 但当他们针锋相对时，就不一样了。

sentences.en: No, that's the difference.
sentences.zh: 不，这就是区别。

sentences.en: These two men who are so important in his life.
sentences.zh: 这两个对他的生命如此重要的人。

sentences.en: It kind of is his ultimate nightmare.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上是他终极的噩梦。

sentences.en: But to reiterate, basically everything else that Johnson has said on this tour, Boswell has written down.
sentences.zh: 但重申一下，基本上约翰逊在此次旅程中所说的其他所有话，博斯韦尔都记下来了。

sentences.en: They are there in his journals.
sentences.zh: 它们都记录在他的日记里。

sentences.en: They are ready to be used.
sentences.zh: 随时准备派上用场。

sentences.en: Johnson has decided on the course of the tour that he's going to write a book.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊在旅程中就已经决定要写一本书。

sentences.en: Boswell has already, even before going on the tour with Johnson, decided that his ultimate ambition is to write a biography of Johnson once Johnson is dead.
sentences.zh: 甚至在和约翰逊一同踏上旅程之前，博斯韦尔就已经决定，他终极的雄心就是在约翰逊死后为他写一本传记。

sentences.en: And so this is one of the reasons why he has been kind of occasionally goading Johnson.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是他偶尔会去激怒约翰逊的原因之一。

sentences.en: He wants, you know, he wants kind of good copy throughout the tour.
sentences.zh: 他希望，你知道的，他希望在整个旅程中都有好的素材。

sentences.en: He's pressing Johnson to tell him details about his life.
sentences.zh: 他催促约翰逊告诉他关于其生平的细节。

sentences.en: And it's almost the case that Johnson is so busy writing up what Johnson says that he doesn't actually have much time to talk to Johnson.
sentences.zh: 甚至可以说，约翰逊太忙于记录约翰逊所说的话了，以至于他实际上没有太多时间跟约翰逊交流。

sentences.en: Johnson and Boswell have both returned from this trip with the kind of raw material for future books that both of them had wanted.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊和博斯韦尔从这次旅行中归来时，都带着他们各自想要的、用于未来书籍的原始素材。

sentences.en: And Boswell absolutely feels, I do now have the material for a kind of a biography of Johnson that will be unlike any biography that has ever been written.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔绝对觉得，我如今确实掌握了为约翰逊写一本传记的素材，这将是一部史无前例的传记。

sentences.en: However, even as he is plotting this, he is aware that he has a rival, someone who actually is more familiar and certainly more intimate with Johnson than Boswell has ever been.
sentences.zh: 然而，就在他精心筹划这一切的同时，他意识到自己有一个竞争对手——一个比博斯韦尔以往任何时候都更熟悉约翰逊、当然也更亲密的人。

sentences.en: And this is a rival who isn't just a woman, but more than that, Dominic, a woman from Wales.
sentences.zh: 这个对手不仅是个女人，不仅如此，多米尼克，还是个来自威尔士的女人。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Well, that is a bombshell.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这真是一个重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: Very exciting.
sentences.zh: 太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: If you're a member of the Rest is History Club, you can get that episode right now.
sentences.zh: 如果你是“历史其余部分”俱乐部的成员，你现在就可以收听那一集。

sentences.en: If you're not and you would like to join our own depopulated Hebridean clan, then please head to therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是，但又想加入我们这个荒凉的赫布里底族群，请访问 therestishistory.com。

sentences.en: So next time on the Rest is History, a sentence I thought I would never say.
sentences.zh: 那么，下期《历史的其余部分》——一句我以为我永远不会说出口的话。

sentences.en: We will be talking about a Welsh woman.
sentences.zh: 我们将聊聊一位威尔士女性。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 拜拜。
